source: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual (Sections B and C), tn.gov/safety

questions.question: What are properly adjusted seat head restraints designed to do?
questions.answer: Prevent whiplash if you are hit from behind
wrong: Keep your head straight when you check mirrors
Hold your head still during a sharp turn
Protect your head if the air bag opens
questions.explanation: Head restraints are designed to prevent whiplash if you are hit from behind. Adjust them level with the back of your head.
questions.manual_quote: Head restraints are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.

questions.question: How high should you adjust the seat head restraint?
questions.answer: Level with the back of your head
wrong: Level with the base of your neck
Level with the top of your shoulders
Just above the top of your head
questions.explanation: Adjust the head restraint to a level even with the back of the head.
questions.manual_quote: Properly adjust seat head restraints to a level even with the back of the head.

questions.question: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?
questions.answer: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
wrong: 11 o'clock and 6 o'clock
7 o'clock and 5 o'clock
10 o'clock and 12 o'clock
questions.explanation: Left hand at 9 o'clock, right hand at 3 o'clock. This position helps avoid injury if the air bag opens.
questions.manual_quote: place the left hand at the 9 o'clock position and the right hand at 3 o'clock position

questions.question: About how far back from the steering wheel should your body be?
questions.answer: 10 to 12 inches
wrong: 6 to 8 inches
18 to 24 inches
3 to 5 inches
questions.explanation: Sit about 10 to 12 inches back. At this distance an air bag hits your chest, not your chin or face.
questions.manual_quote: Your body should be about 10 to 12 inches back from the steering wheel with or without an air bag.

questions.question: What is the highest the top of the steering wheel should be?
questions.answer: No higher than the top of your shoulders
wrong: No higher than the top of your head
No higher than your chin
No higher than the middle of your chest
questions.explanation: The top of the steering wheel should be no higher than the top of your shoulders.
questions.manual_quote: The top of the steering wheel should be no higher than the top of the shoulders.

questions.question: Why should you NOT drive with the seat reclined or semi-reclined?
questions.answer: It reduces your vision and your ability to react
wrong: It makes the air bag open too slowly during a crash
It makes the seat belt lock while driving
It makes the mirrors impossible to adjust
questions.explanation: Driving reclined is dangerous because it reduces both your vision and your ability to react to emergencies.
questions.manual_quote: This is dangerous and reduces both your vision and your ability to react to emergency situations.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.answer: After you adjust the seat, and before you start driving
wrong: Before you adjust the seat, so the seat does not move them
While you are driving at a slow speed
After you start moving and pull onto the main road
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors after your seat is adjusted correctly. Always adjust them before you start driving.
questions.manual_quote: Adjust mirrors after the seat is adjusted correctly. (Always adjust before driving.)

questions.question: How should you adjust the inside rearview mirror?
questions.answer: So it frames the rear window
wrong: So it shows the back seat
So it shows the right side of the car
So it shows the road surface behind you
questions.explanation: Adjust the inside rearview mirror to frame the rear window.
questions.manual_quote: Adjust the inside rearview mirror to frame the rear window.

questions.question: To set your left side mirror, where do you put your head?
questions.answer: Against the left side window
wrong: Just above the center console
Against the head restraint
Over your right shoulder
questions.explanation: Sit upright, put your head against the left window, and set the mirror so you can just barely see the side of your car.
questions.manual_quote: seated in an upright position place your head against the left side window and adjust the left side mirror.

questions.question: To set your right side mirror, where do you put your head?
questions.answer: Just above the center console
wrong: Against the left side window
Against the right side window
Leaning back against the seat
questions.explanation: Position your head just above the center console, then set the mirror so you just barely see the side of your car.
questions.manual_quote: position your head so that it is just above the center console.

questions.question: Your mirrors are adjusted correctly. What must you still do before you turn or change lanes?
questions.answer: Turn your head and check your blind spots
wrong: Look only in the inside mirror
Look only in the side mirrors
Tap the horn to warn any drivers who are beside you
questions.explanation: Even properly adjusted mirrors cannot remove all blind spots. Always turn your head and check.
questions.manual_quote: always turn your head and check blind spots when you want to turn or change lanes.

questions.question: How should your foot move from the accelerator to the brake?
questions.answer: Smoothly, with your heel kept on the floor
wrong: Quickly, with your foot lifted high
Slowly, using your left foot instead
Smoothly, with your toes kept on the floor
questions.explanation: Your foot should move smoothly from the accelerator to the brake while the heel stays on the floor.
questions.manual_quote: Your foot should move smoothly from the accelerator to the brake while the heel is kept on the floor.

questions.question: Where should a lap belt be positioned?
questions.answer: Firmly across the hips
wrong: Loosely across the stomach
Firmly across the ribs
Loosely across the knees
questions.explanation: Lap belts go firmly across the hips. The shoulder belt goes firmly across the shoulder.
questions.manual_quote: Lap belts should be positioned firmly across the hips while the shoulder belt is firmly across the shoulder.

questions.question: Is it legal to coast downhill with the gears in neutral?
questions.answer: No, coasting in neutral is illegal
wrong: Yes, on hills that are not steep
Yes, if no other cars are nearby
Yes, if the speed stays under 25 mph
questions.explanation: Don't coast with the gears in neutral. It is illegal.
questions.manual_quote: Don't coast with the gears in neutral (it's illegal)

questions.question: What should you do when going down a steep hill?
questions.answer: Shift into a lower gear
wrong: Shift into neutral
Shift into the highest gear (overdrive)
Turn off the engine
questions.explanation: When going down steep hills, place the vehicle in a lower gear.
questions.manual_quote: When going down steep hills, place the vehicle in a lower gear.

questions.question: What is the basic rule for a car with a steering wheel interlock system?
questions.answer: Never turn the ignition to LOCK while the car is moving
wrong: Always keep the ignition in LOCK while the car is parked
Never steer the car before the engine is warm
Always turn the key to LOCK just before the car stops
questions.explanation: If you turn the ignition to LOCK while the car is moving, the steering wheel will lock when you try to turn, and you will lose control of the car.
questions.manual_quote: never turn the ignition to the lock position when the vehicle is in motion

questions.question: Before starting a car with an automatic transmission, where should the gearshift be?
questions.answer: In PARK, with your foot on the brake
wrong: In DRIVE, with your foot on the brake
In NEUTRAL, with your foot on the gas
In REVERSE, with the parking brake off
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, put your foot on the brake and make sure the gearshift is in PARK. In a car with a manual transmission, it should be in NEUTRAL.
questions.manual_quote: ensure gearshift selector is in the PARK position for automatic transmissions

questions.question: In normal daylight, how much farther away can other people see your car when your headlights are on?
questions.answer: Twice the distance
wrong: Three times the distance
Four times the distance
One and a half times the distance
questions.explanation: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.
questions.manual_quote: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.

questions.question: When are the lower gears (L, 2, or 1) on an automatic transmission used?
questions.answer: Going down steep hills, driving slowly on ice, or if the brakes fail
wrong: Driving in normal city traffic that has a lot of stops and starts
Driving on the highway when there is little stop-and-go traffic
Starting the car on a cold morning
questions.explanation: Lower gears are only for special cases: driving down steep mountain grades, driving slowly on icy or slippery roads, or slowing down in an emergency if the brakes fail.
questions.manual_quote: Driving down steep mountain grades. Slow speed driving on icy or other slippery roads. Emergency deceleration if there is a brake failure.

questions.question: What is the "O" (overdrive) gear on some cars for?
questions.answer: Driving on interstates with very little stop-and-go traffic
wrong: Driving down steep mountain grades and long hills
Driving slowly on icy roads
Backing up a long driveway
questions.explanation: Overdrive is for driving on interstates or expressways where there is very little stop-and-go traffic.
questions.manual_quote: for use when driving on interstates or other expressways where there is very little stop and go traffic.

questions.question: In a manual transmission car, when do you hold the clutch pedal all the way down?
questions.answer: When you start, when you shift, and when you slow below 10 mph to stop
wrong: Only when the car is going uphill and you need more power
Only while you are cruising at speeds above 10 mph
Only when you are parked and the engine is turned off
questions.explanation: Hold the clutch pedal all the way down when you start, when you shift gears, and when your speed drops below 10 mph as you come to a stop.
questions.manual_quote: Hold the clutch pedal all the way down when starting, shifting gears and when speed drops below 10 MPH

questions.question: What does "riding the clutch" mean?
questions.answer: Resting your foot on the clutch when not shifting
wrong: Shifting gears without using the clutch
Pressing the clutch and brake together
Letting the clutch pedal out too quickly after shifting
questions.explanation: Riding the clutch means driving with your foot resting on the clutch pedal when you do not need to change gears. Do not ride the clutch.
questions.manual_quote: don't drive with your foot resting on the clutch pedal if it is not needed to change gears.

questions.question: Which steering method does the manual recommend for normal everyday driving?
questions.answer: Push-Pull
wrong: Hand-over-Hand
One-hand steering
Palm steering
questions.explanation: Push-Pull is recommended. It makes smoother turns and keeps both hands on the wheel the whole time.
questions.manual_quote: the Push-Pull method is recommended for normal everyday driving.

questions.question: Why should you NOT cross your arms when steering?
questions.answer: You would be hurt more if the air bag opens
wrong: It makes the car turn much too slowly in tight spaces
It makes the turn signal cancel early
It blocks your view of the gauges
questions.explanation: Crossing your wrists while turning is OK, but crossing your arms is not. Clothing and jewelry can get in the way of a safe turn, and you would be hurt worse if the air bag opens.
questions.manual_quote: you would suffer more serious injuries should the air bag deploy.

questions.question: When backing up in a car with an automatic transmission, how should you hold the wheel and look?
questions.answer: Left hand at 12 o'clock, looking back over your right shoulder
wrong: Both hands at 9 and 3 o'clock, looking only in the inside mirror
Right hand at 12 o'clock, looking in the left mirror
Left hand at 6 o'clock, looking in the side mirrors
questions.explanation: Grasp the wheel at 12 o'clock with your left hand, turn right, put your right arm over the seat, and look through the rear window.
questions.manual_quote: Grasp steering wheel at 12 o'clock position with left hand.

questions.question: When backing up, how long should you keep looking to the rear?
questions.answer: Until you come to a complete stop
wrong: Until the car starts moving
Until you have backed one car length
Until you are halfway out of the space
questions.explanation: Keep looking to the rear until you come to a complete stop.
questions.manual_quote: Continue looking to the rear until coming to a complete stop.

questions.question: When pulling forward from a stop, how far ahead should you look?
questions.answer: At least one block ahead
wrong: Just past the front bumper
At least one mile ahead
At the car directly in front
questions.explanation: Look at least one block ahead and steer toward a reference point.
questions.manual_quote: Look at least one block ahead and steer toward a reference point.

questions.question: When stopping at a curb to park, how close should you get?
questions.answer: Within 18 inches of the curb
wrong: Within 36 inches of the curb
Within 6 feet of the curb
Within 30 inches of the curb
questions.explanation: Move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.
questions.manual_quote: If stopping at a curb, move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.

questions.question: When stopping at a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
questions.answer: Where you can see cross traffic, before entering the intersection
wrong: In the middle of the intersection
After your front bumper has moved past the edge of the cross street
Wherever the car ahead of you stopped
questions.explanation: Stop before the crosswalk or stop line. If there is none, stop where you can see approaching traffic, before entering the intersection.
questions.manual_quote: at the point of the nearest intersecting roadway, where you can view the approaching traffic

questions.question: What is the most common type of crash in Tennessee?
questions.answer: Rear-end collisions
wrong: Head-on collisions
Side-impact collisions
Single-car rollovers
questions.explanation: Rear-end collisions are the most common type. Planning ahead for smooth stops helps avoid them.
questions.manual_quote: Tennessee reports that rear-end collisions are the most common type of accident recorded annually.

questions.question: How should you press the brake for a normal stop?
questions.answer: With steady pressure, without stomping on it
wrong: With quick, hard taps on the pedal until stopped
With one hard stomp
With your left foot only
questions.explanation: Press the brake with steady pressure for a smooth stop. Do not stomp on the brake.
questions.manual_quote: Press down on the brake pedal with a steady pressure for a smooth stop. Do not "stomp" on the brake pedal.

questions.question: How can you tell if carbon monoxide is in your car?
questions.answer: You can't tell, because it has no taste, smell, or color
wrong: It has a strong smell like rotten eggs or gasoline
It looks like a light gray smoke
It tastes bitter in your mouth
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide from an engine can kill. It has no taste, no smell, and cannot be seen.
questions.manual_quote: Carbon monoxide gas from a car engine can kill (it has not taste, no smell or visibility).

questions.question: When does carbon monoxide generally leak into a car?
questions.answer: When the heater is running or the exhaust system is not working right
wrong: When the windows are rolled down on the open highway
When the gas tank is nearly full
When the air bag warning light on the dashboard is on
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide generally leaks in when the heater is running, when the exhaust system is not working right, or in heavy traffic when you breathe fumes from other cars.
questions.manual_quote: It generally leaks when the car heater is running, when the exhaust system is not working properly

questions.question: Which of these helps prevent carbon monoxide poisoning?
questions.answer: Never let the engine run in a closed garage
wrong: Open the fresh-air vent in heavy traffic
Run the heater in a parked car with windows up
Only check the exhaust system once it gets loud
questions.explanation: Never run the engine in a closed garage. Also, check the exhaust system regularly, and close the fresh-air vent in heavy traffic.
questions.manual_quote: Never let the engine run in a closed garage

questions.question: In congested traffic, what should you do with the fresh-air vent to avoid carbon monoxide?
questions.answer: Close it
wrong: Open it all the way
Set it to the defrost setting
Switch it to the floor vents
questions.explanation: Close the fresh-air vent in congested traffic so you don't breathe other vehicles' fumes.
questions.manual_quote: Close the fresh-air vent in congested traffic

questions.question: Under Tennessee's Hands Free law, which is illegal for a driver?
questions.answer: Holding a phone with any part of your body
wrong: Listening to the radio while driving
Talking on the phone in hands-free mode
Using the car's built-in rear camera
questions.explanation: It is illegal to hold a phone with any part of your body, to text, to watch video, or to record or broadcast video while driving.
questions.manual_quote: (a) hold a cellphone or mobile device with any part of their body,

questions.question: Under Tennessee's Hands Free law, is a driver allowed to watch a video on a phone?
questions.answer: No, watching video on a phone is illegal
wrong: Yes, if the phone is held in a dashboard mount
Yes, if the car is in the right lane
Yes, if the sound is turned off
questions.explanation: The Hands Free law makes it illegal to watch a video or movie on a phone or mobile device.
questions.manual_quote: (d) watch a video or movie on a cellphone or mobile device

questions.question: Under Tennessee's Hands Free law, can a driver reach for a phone in a way that takes them out of the seated driving position?
questions.answer: No, that is illegal
wrong: Yes, if traffic is light
Yes, if it is an emergency call
Yes, if the phone is on the floor
questions.explanation: It is illegal to reach for a phone in a way that means you are no longer seated or properly belted.
questions.manual_quote: reach for a cellphone or mobile device in a manner that requires the driver to no longer be in a seated driving position

questions.question: What is the maximum fine for texting on a hand-held phone while driving?
questions.answer: A fine of up to $50, plus up to $10 in court costs
wrong: A fine of up to $100, plus up to $20 in court costs
A fine of up to $25, plus up to $5 in court costs
A fine of up to $200, plus up to $50 in court costs
questions.explanation: A violation can bring a fine of up to $50, plus court costs of up to $10.
questions.manual_quote: Violations can result in a fine not to exceed Fifty Dollars, and court costs not to exceed Ten Dollars.

questions.question: Who is exempt from the texting-while-driving law?
questions.answer: Police, firefighters, and emergency medical workers on official duty
wrong: Any driver who is stopped and waiting at a red light
Any driver who is over the age of 21
Any driver who has a full driver license
questions.explanation: Police officers, firefighters, emergency medical workers, and emergency management officers are exempt, but only while they are doing their official duties.
questions.manual_quote: Law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency medical persons and emergency management agency officers

questions.question: When is it an offense for a driver 18 or older to use a hand-held phone in a school zone?
questions.answer: When the school zone warning flashers are on
wrong: Only on days when school buses are running their routes
Only when children are in the crosswalk
Only between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m.
questions.explanation: For drivers 18 or older, it is an offense to use a hand-held phone while moving in a marked school zone when the warning flashers are on. Using the phone in hands-free mode is allowed.
questions.manual_quote: in any marked school zone in this state, when a warning flasher or flashers are in operation.

questions.question: A driver under 18 uses a phone in hands-free mode in a school zone with flashers on. Is this allowed?
questions.answer: No, the hands-free exception does not apply to drivers under 18
wrong: Yes, hands-free is allowed for every driver
Yes, if the driver has a learner permit
Yes, as long as a parent or guardian is riding in the car
questions.explanation: The hands-free exception does not apply to drivers under 18. For them, using a phone in a school zone with the flashers on is a delinquent act.
questions.manual_quote: This exception also does not apply to persons under eighteen (18) years of age

questions.question: Which video screen is allowed to be visible to the driver while the car is moving?
questions.answer: A navigation (GPS) display
wrong: A screen showing a TV broadcast
A screen playing a movie
A screen showing a video signal from a phone
questions.explanation: State law bans video screens that the driver can see if they show TV or video. Navigation (GPS) displays, vehicle information, and camera views are allowed.
questions.manual_quote: A navigation or global positioning device, a vehicle information system display

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt any time the vehicle is moving?
questions.answer: The driver and all front-seat passengers
wrong: Only the driver
Only the driver and passengers who are under 18
Only passengers in the back seat
questions.explanation: Safety belts are required for ALL drivers and all front-seat passengers any time the vehicle is in motion.
questions.manual_quote: Safety belts are required for ALL drivers and all passengers in the FRONT seat, any time the vehicle is in motion.

questions.question: Can a Tennessee officer stop you only because you are not wearing a safety belt?
questions.answer: Yes, they can stop and ticket you for that alone
wrong: No, only if you are also breaking another traffic law
No, they can only give you a warning
No, only if a child is riding in the car
questions.explanation: Officers can stop you and give you a ticket only because you are not obeying the safety belt or child restraint laws.
questions.manual_quote: Officers can stop and ticket drivers solely for disobeying Safety belt and Child Restraint Device (CRD) laws.

questions.question: If the driver has a learner permit or intermediate license, which back-seat passengers must wear belts?
questions.answer: Passengers between four and 17 years old
wrong: Only passengers who are under four years old
Only passengers over 18 years old
No back-seat passengers
questions.explanation: With a learner permit or intermediate license driver, back-seat passengers between 4 and 17 must be belted.
questions.manual_quote: If the driver has either a learner permit or an intermediate license, and when the passengers are between four and 17 years old.

questions.question: A child under one year old, or under 20 pounds, must ride in what kind of seat?
questions.answer: A rear-facing car seat
wrong: A forward-facing car seat
A booster seat with a lap belt
A regular seat with a safety belt
questions.explanation: A child under 1 or under 20 pounds must be in a car seat facing the rear of the car.
questions.manual_quote: must be in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) that is facing the rear of the car.

questions.question: A child one through three years old, weighing more than 20 pounds, must ride in what kind of seat?
questions.answer: A forward-facing car seat
wrong: A rear-facing car seat
A booster seat
A regular seat with a safety belt
questions.explanation: Children 1 through 3 who weigh more than 20 pounds must be in a forward-facing car seat.
questions.manual_quote: must be in a child passenger restraint system that is facing forward.

questions.question: Which statement about car seats is correct?
questions.answer: Rear-facing if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Forward-facing if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
wrong: Forward-facing if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Rear-facing if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
Rear-facing if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Booster seat if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
Booster seat if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Seat belt only if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
questions.explanation: A child under 1 year old, or any child under 20 pounds, must ride rear-facing. Children 1 through 3 years old who weigh more than 20 pounds must ride forward-facing.
questions.manual_quote: facing the rear of the car... one through three years old, and who weigh more than 20 pounds... facing forward.

questions.question: A child four through eight years old and shorter than 4 feet 9 inches must ride in what?
questions.answer: A booster seat and a seat belt
wrong: A rear-facing car seat
A seat belt with no booster
A forward-facing car seat with harness
questions.explanation: Children 4 through 8 and under 4'9" must be in a belt-positioning booster seat and wear a seat belt.
questions.manual_quote: must be in a belt positioning booster seat system (child booster car seat) and wearing a seatbelt.

questions.question: Where must a child in a booster seat ride, if the car has a back seat?
questions.answer: In the back seat
wrong: In the front passenger seat
In whichever seat has an air bag
In the seat behind the driver only
questions.explanation: Children in booster seats must be in the back seat of a vehicle if it has a back seat.
questions.manual_quote: Children in booster seats must be in the back seat of a vehicle, if the vehicle has a back seat.

questions.question: The driver is responsible for properly restraining children up to what age?
questions.explanation: The law makes the driver responsible for children's protection up to age 16.
questions.manual_quote: makes the driver responsible for their protection up to the age of sixteen (16).

questions.question: What is the fine if children under 16 are not properly restrained?
questions.explanation: The driver may be charged and fined $50.
questions.manual_quote: the driver may be charged and fined $50.00 for violation of the law.

questions.question: A child's parent is riding in the car but not driving. Who is responsible for the child being properly restrained?
questions.answer: The parent or legal guardian
wrong: The driver only
The child
No one, if the parent is present
questions.explanation: If the parent or legal guardian is in the car but not driving, the parent is responsible and may be fined.
questions.manual_quote: then the parent or legal guardian is responsible for making sure that the child is properly transported

questions.question: Not using a car seat or booster seat for a child under 9 (or under 4'9") can be charged as what?
questions.answer: A Class C misdemeanor
wrong: A Class A felony
A traffic warning only
A Class B felony
questions.explanation: Not using a car seat or booster seat for a child under 9 (or shorter than 4 feet 9 inches) has a bigger penalty. The driver can be charged with a Class C misdemeanor, must take a class on safely transporting children, and may have to pay fees and fines.
questions.manual_quote: The driver can be charged with a Class C misdemeanor

questions.question: A child uses a medically prescribed modified car seat. What should be kept in the vehicle?
questions.answer: A copy of the doctor's prescription
wrong: The car seat's original sales receipt
A letter from the child's school
A note from the car dealer
questions.explanation: A copy of a doctor's prescription should be carried in the vehicle at all times.
questions.manual_quote: A copy of a doctor's prescription should be carried in the vehicle

questions.question: How should the lap belt be worn?
questions.answer: Low over the pelvis, touching the tops of the thighs
wrong: High across the stomach for comfort
Above the pelvis so it doesn't touch the tops of the thighs
Loosely across the lower ribs
questions.explanation: The lap belt should be worn low over the pelvis with its bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs snugly.
questions.manual_quote: The lap belt should be worn low over the pelvis with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs snugly.

questions.question: How should a pregnant woman wear her safety belt?
questions.answer: Lap belt below the abdomen, shoulder belt above the belly
wrong: Lap belt across the middle of the belly, shoulder belt under the arm
Only the lap belt, without the shoulder belt
Only the shoulder belt, without the lap belt
questions.explanation: Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.
questions.manual_quote: Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

questions.question: Where should the shoulder belt be worn?
questions.answer: Over the shoulder and across the chest
wrong: Under the arm and across the abdomen for comfort
Behind your back
Across your neck
questions.explanation: The shoulder belt goes over the shoulder and across the chest, not under the arm.
questions.manual_quote: The shoulder belt should be worn over the shoulder and across the chest, not under the arm

questions.question: In a side crash, which way do unbelted passengers slide?
questions.answer: Toward the point of the crash
wrong: Away from the point of the crash
Straight forward
Straight up toward the roof
questions.explanation: Everything not fastened down, including passengers, slides toward the point of the crash, not away from it.
questions.manual_quote: will slide toward the point of the crash, not away from it.

questions.question: Compared to people who stay inside, how much more likely are ejected occupants to be killed?
questions.answer: Four times
wrong: Two times
Ten times
One and a half times
questions.explanation: Ejected occupants are four times more likely to be killed than those who remain inside the vehicle.
questions.manual_quote: Ejected occupants are four times more likely to be killed as those who remain inside the vehicle.

questions.question: When is a child big enough to use the regular lap and shoulder belt?
questions.answer: When they can sit all the way back and their knees bend over the seat edge
wrong: When they turn six years old, no matter how tall they are
When they weigh at least 40 pounds
When their feet can rest flat on the car floor in front of them
questions.explanation: A child can use the regular lap and shoulder belt when they can sit with their back against the seat back and their knees bend over the edge of the seat.
questions.manual_quote: they can sit with their back against the vehicle seat back and (2) their knees bend over the edge of the vehicle seat.

questions.question: Where should the shoulder belt rest on a child?
questions.answer: Across the chest, between the neck and shoulder
wrong: Behind the child's back so it does not rub the neck
Under the child's arm
Across the child's face
questions.explanation: The shoulder belt should fit snugly across the chest and rest between the neck and shoulder. Never put it behind the back or under the arms.
questions.manual_quote: The shoulder belt should fit snugly across the chest and rest between the neck and shoulder.

questions.question: "Belts to Bones": which bones should take the pressure of the safety belt?
questions.answer: The pelvic bone and the collarbone
wrong: The lower ribs and the soft part of the stomach
The neck and the shoulder blade
The spine and the hip
questions.explanation: The pelvic bone and the collarbone should bear the pressure. If the belt rides on the stomach or neck, go back to a booster seat.
questions.manual_quote: The pelvic bone and the collarbone should bear the pressure of the safety belts.

questions.question: The safety belt rides high on a child's stomach. What should you do?
questions.answer: Go back to using a booster seat
wrong: Tuck the shoulder belt behind the child
Move the child to the front seat
Loosen the lap belt for comfort
questions.explanation: If the belt rides too high on the stomach or the shoulder belt crosses the face or neck, go back to a booster seat.
questions.manual_quote: go back to using a booster seat or a high back booster model

questions.question: It is illegal for a child under what age to ride in the bed of a pickup truck?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to let any child under 6 ride in a pickup truck bed. Children 6 through 12 also may not ride there on state or interstate highways.
questions.manual_quote: It is illegal in Tennessee to allow any child under the age of 6 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck.

questions.question: Children under 6 may never ride in a pickup truck bed. On a state or interstate highway, which older children are also not allowed to ride there?
questions.answer: Ages 6 through 12
wrong: Ages 13 through 16
