wrong: Any driver who will be parked there for less than 15 minutes
Any driver with a passenger over 65
Any driver if the lot is full
questions.explanation: These spaces are only for vehicles with disabled veteran plates, handicapped plates, or a special decal. The law does not allow anyone else to park there.
questions.manual_quote: reserved for vehicles bearing disabled veteran or handicapped license plates, or a special handicapped decal.

questions.question: How often are emergency reference markers placed on busy urban interstates?
questions.answer: Every 1,000 feet
wrong: Every 500 feet
Every mile
Every 10,000 feet
questions.explanation: They are installed every 1,000 feet on heavily traveled sections to help you tell emergency operators your exact location.
questions.manual_quote: the state has installed interstate reference markers every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled sections.

questions.question: What do emergency reference markers help you do?
questions.answer: Tell 911 your exact location on the interstate
wrong: Find the nearest gas station or restaurant off the exit
Know the speed limit ahead
Find the next rest area
questions.explanation: They show route number, direction, and log mile so you can give emergency operators an accurate location.
questions.manual_quote: can give an accurate description of the exact location where assistance is needed.

questions.question: What is the order of lights on a standard traffic signal, from top to bottom?
questions.answer: Red, yellow, green
wrong: Green, yellow, red
Yellow, red, green
Red, green, yellow
questions.explanation: Standard traffic lights are red, yellow, and green from top to bottom.
questions.manual_quote: Standard traffic lights are red, yellow and green, from top to bottom respectively.

questions.question: At a red light, where should you stop?
questions.answer: Behind the crosswalk or stop line
wrong: In the crosswalk
Past the stop line
Halfway into the intersection, where you can see
questions.explanation: At a red light, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line.
questions.manual_quote: RED: Stop behind crosswalk or stop line.

questions.question: Unless a sign says otherwise, may you turn right on a red light?
questions.answer: Yes, after a complete stop, if there are no pedestrians or cross traffic
wrong: No, never on a red light
Yes, without stopping if the road is clear
Yes, but only between midnight and 6 a.m. when traffic is light
questions.explanation: Unless posted otherwise, you may turn right on red after a complete stop when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.
questions.manual_quote: you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

questions.question: What should you do when a steady yellow light appears?
questions.answer: Slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely
wrong: Speed up to get through before it turns red
Keep going at the same speed
Slam on the brakes, even if you are already in the intersection
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light is about to turn red. Slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Do not speed up to try to get through before the light turns red.
questions.manual_quote: You must stop if it is safe to do so. Do not speed up to beat the light.

questions.question: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow. What should you do?
questions.answer: Continue cautiously through the intersection
wrong: Stop right where you are and wait for the next green
Back up out of the intersection
Speed up to beat the red light
questions.explanation: If you are already IN the intersection when the yellow comes on, do not stop—continue cautiously through.
questions.manual_quote: If you are already IN the intersection when the yellow light comes on, do not stop, but continue cautiously through the intersection.

questions.question: Tennessee law requires the yellow light to show for at least how long before the red light?
questions.answer: 3 seconds
wrong: 2 seconds
5 seconds
10 seconds
questions.explanation: Tennessee law requires the yellow light to show for at least three seconds before the light turns red.
questions.manual_quote: Tennessee law only requires the yellow light to be exhibited for a minimum of three seconds before the red light.

questions.question: Your light turns green. What must you still do?
questions.answer: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection
wrong: Go immediately, because a green light gives you the right of way
Honk to clear the intersection
Wait three seconds before moving
questions.explanation: Green means go IF the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.
questions.manual_quote: GREEN: Go IF the intersection is clear. You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection at light change.

questions.question: You have a green light (not an arrow) and want to turn left. Who must you yield to?
questions.answer: Oncoming vehicles
wrong: No one, because green gives you the right-of-way
Only vehicles behind you
Only vehicles turning right
questions.explanation: The green signal gives permission to go, but you must yield to oncoming vehicles if turning left.
questions.manual_quote: Yield to oncoming vehicles if you are turning left.

questions.question: What does a green turn arrow (protected turn) mean?
questions.answer: You may turn that way, and you have the right-of-way
wrong: You must yield to all oncoming traffic before you turn
You may go in any direction
You must stop, then turn
questions.explanation: When the arrow is green you have the right of way and may go only in the arrow's direction, after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.manual_quote: When the arrow is green, you have the right-of-way and may drive the vehicle only in the direction of the arrow

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow mean?
questions.answer: Your protected turn is ending, so get ready to yield
wrong: You may turn left with the right-of-way
You must stop now and wait for the next green light
Oncoming traffic must stop for you
questions.explanation: When the arrow changes to yellow, the protected turn is about to end. Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.manual_quote: When the arrow changes to yellow, prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your lane has a red arrow, but other lanes have green and the path looks clear. May you turn?
questions.answer: No, all turns are prohibited
wrong: Yes, if the path through the intersection is clear
Yes, after a complete stop
Yes, if you signal first
questions.explanation: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited, even if other lanes have green.
questions.manual_quote: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean?
questions.answer: Turn left after yielding to oncoming cars and pedestrians
wrong: You have the right-of-way to turn left, and oncoming cars must stop
You may not turn left at all
You must stop before turning left
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Wait for a safe gap.
questions.manual_quote: If you see a flashing yellow arrow, you are allowed to turn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?
questions.answer: Come to a complete stop, like a stop sign
wrong: Slow down and go with caution
Stop only if you see cross traffic coming toward you
Treat it as a yield sign
questions.explanation: Flashing red means a complete stop, the same as a stop sign. Look both ways, yield, and go when safe.
questions.manual_quote: FLASHING RED Complete stop. Same as stop sign.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
questions.answer: Slow down and go through with caution
wrong: Come to a complete stop, just like at a stop sign
Speed up to clear the intersection
Stop and wait for a green light
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.manual_quote: FLASHING YELLOW Slow down and proceed with caution

questions.question: When should you pull into a busy intersection to make a turn?
questions.answer: Only when your path is clear
wrong: As soon as your light turns green
Whenever the car ahead of you moves
Whenever you can get halfway across
questions.explanation: Do not pull into an intersection to make a turn until your path is clear, so you don't get stranded inside it.
questions.manual_quote: do not pull into an intersection to make a turn until your path is clear.

questions.question: A traffic signal is not working at all. What does Tennessee law require?
questions.answer: Treat it as an all-way stop
wrong: Treat it as a yield for everyone
Go through if you are on the bigger road
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: If a signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop.
questions.manual_quote: if a signal is not working, the intersection is to be treated as if it were a ll-way stop intersection.

questions.question: Two vehicles stop at an all-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?
questions.answer: The driver on the right
wrong: The driver on the left
The larger vehicle
The driver going straight
questions.explanation: If two or more vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
questions.manual_quote: the driver on the left would yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: How does Tennessee law define a pedestrian?
questions.answer: Any person on foot or using a wheelchair
wrong: Any person on foot only
Any person riding a bicycle on the sidewalk
Any person under age 16 on foot
questions.explanation: Tennessee law defines a pedestrian as any person on foot or using a wheelchair, whether it is motorized or not.
questions.manual_quote: Tennessee law defines a pedestrian as any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair.

questions.question: What does a pedestrian "WALK" signal or walking person symbol mean?
questions.answer: It is safe for pedestrians to cross
wrong: Pedestrians should not start crossing
Drivers may turn without looking
The light is about to turn red
questions.explanation: WALK or a walking person symbol shows when it is safe to cross. People already crossing should keep going quickly.
questions.manual_quote: displays the word "WALK" or a symbol of a person walking when it is safe to cross the street or intersection.

questions.question: What does a "DON'T WALK" signal or raised hand symbol mean?
questions.answer: It is not safe to begin crossing
wrong: Pedestrians may cross with caution
Pedestrians have the right of way
Drivers must stop for the next minute
questions.explanation: DON'T WALK or a raised hand means it is not safe to begin crossing the street.
questions.manual_quote: or a symbol of a raised hand appears, it is not safe to begin crossing a street or intersection.

questions.question: When are lane control signals over the road most often used?
questions.answer: When traffic flow direction changes at different hours
wrong: When the whole road ahead is closed to traffic for repairs
When there is a school zone ahead
When the speed limit changes
questions.explanation: Lane control signals are most often used when the direction of traffic flow changes during different hours. They also show if toll lanes are open.
questions.manual_quote: They are most often used when the direction of the flow of traffic changes during different hours of the day.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the right side of the road show?
questions.answer: The right edge of the traffic lane
wrong: The center of a two-way road
A line you may cross to pass slower cars
The left edge of your lane
questions.explanation: A solid white line shows the right edge of the traffic lane. A yellow line marks the left edge of lanes going your direction.
questions.manual_quote: A solid white line indicates the right edge of the traffic lane on a road.

questions.question: You have a yellow line on your right and a white line on your left. What does this mean?
questions.answer: You are going the wrong way
wrong: You are in the correct lane
You are in a passing zone
You are in a turn lane
questions.explanation: If you find yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.
questions.manual_quote: If you ever find yourself with yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.

questions.question: On a divided highway, what color line is on the left side, nearest the median?
questions.answer: Yellow
wrong: White
Blue
Orange
questions.explanation: On a divided highway, the side to the driver's left and nearest the median always has a yellow line.
questions.manual_quote: the side of the roadway to the left of the driver and nearest the median always has a yellow line.

questions.question: What color lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.answer: Yellow
wrong: White
Blue
Orange
questions.explanation: Lines separating traffic moving in opposite directions are yellow.
questions.manual_quote: Lines separating traffic moving in opposite directions are yellow.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow center line mean?
questions.answer: You may pass if no traffic is coming and it is safe
wrong: You may never cross it
You may cross only to turn right
Traffic on both sides of the line goes the same direction
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines mean you MAY cross to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.
questions.manual_quote: you MAY cross the line to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines between lanes mean?
questions.answer: No passing from either direction
wrong: Passing allowed from either direction
Passing allowed only from the left side
Passing allowed when no cars are coming
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean you MAY NOT cross from either direction, even if no oncoming traffic is in view.
questions.manual_quote: Two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic mean you MAY NOT cross the lines from either direction

questions.question: Can you ever cross a solid yellow line?
questions.answer: Yes, to turn into a driveway or side road if safe
wrong: No, never for any reason
Yes, to pass a slow-moving car if no traffic is coming
Yes, any time no cars are coming
questions.explanation: You may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road if it is safe.
questions.manual_quote: You may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The center has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The broken line is on your side. What does this mean?
questions.answer: You may pass when it is safe
wrong: You are not allowed to pass here, even if no traffic is coming
You may only make right turns here
You must drive below the speed limit
questions.explanation: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in the passing zone and may pass when it is safe. If the solid line is on your side, you may not pass.
questions.manual_quote: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in the "passing zone" and may pass

questions.question: The center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line. The solid line is on your side. May you pass?
questions.answer: No, you may not pass
wrong: Yes, if no cars are coming
Yes, but only on a straight road
Yes, if the car ahead is slow
questions.explanation: You may not pass when the solid yellow line is on your side of the road.
questions.manual_quote: you may not pass if the solid yellow line is on your side.

questions.question: After passing in a passing zone, when must you be back on your side of the road?
questions.answer: Before the passing zone ends
wrong: Within one mile after you pass
Before you reach the next intersection
Whenever it feels comfortable to you
questions.explanation: You must safely return to your side of the road before the passing zone ends.
questions.manual_quote: You must safely return to your side of the roadway before the passing zone ends.

questions.question: What color lines separate lanes of traffic going the same direction?
questions.answer: White
wrong: Yellow
Blue
Orange
questions.explanation: Multiple lanes of traffic flowing in the same direction are separated by white lane markings.
questions.manual_quote: Multiple lanes of traffic that flow in the same direction are separated by white lane markings.

questions.question: What do broken white lines between lanes mean?
questions.answer: You may change lanes or pass if it is safe
wrong: You may never change lanes
Traffic on the other side is going the opposite way
The lane is ending soon
questions.explanation: Broken white lines mean you may cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.
questions.manual_quote: Broken white lines between lanes of traffic mean you may cross the lines to pass or change lanes

questions.question: What does one solid white line between lanes mean?
questions.answer: Stay in your lane unless there is an emergency
wrong: You may pass whenever it is safe
Traffic on the other side goes the opposite way
You must change lanes soon
questions.explanation: A solid white line means stay in your lane and do not cross it to pass, unless an emergency makes you. Never cross a double solid white line.
questions.manual_quote: you should stay in your lane and should not cross the line to pass

questions.question: When must you yield to pedestrians at a crosswalk?
questions.answer: When they are in or about to enter the crosswalk
wrong: Only when they are in the middle of the street
Only at crosswalks that have a WALK signal showing
Only at marked crosswalks
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians who are in or about to enter the crosswalk or street. Not all crosswalks are marked.
questions.manual_quote: yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are in or are about to enter the crosswalk or street.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or marked crosswalk, where must you stop?
questions.answer: Before your front bumper crosses the cross street's white edge line
wrong: With your front bumper already in the cross street
After your front bumper passes the cross street's white edge line
Wherever you can see best, even out in the street
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before your front bumper crosses the white edge line of the cross street.
questions.manual_quote: Stop the vehicle before the front bumper crosses the white edge line of the cross street

questions.question: If there is no stop line but there is a marked crosswalk, where do you stop?
questions.answer: Before the first line of the crosswalk
wrong: On top of the crosswalk
Just past the crosswalk, at the edge of the cross street
At the far side of the intersection
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing the first line of the crosswalk.
questions.manual_quote: Stop the vehicle before crossing the first line of the crosswalk (if the crosswalk is marked)

questions.question: How is an HOV lane marked on the pavement?
questions.answer: With a diamond shape in the center of the lane
wrong: With a white arrow
With a yellow X
With a white bicycle symbol painted in the center
questions.explanation: HOV lanes are marked by a diamond-shaped marking in the center of the lane.
questions.manual_quote: Lanes are designated on highways by a diamond-shaped marking in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Your lane has a curved arrow and the word ONLY. What must you do?
questions.answer: Turn in the direction of the arrow
wrong: Go straight or turn
Turn the opposite way
Change lanes before the intersection
questions.explanation: In a lane marked with a curved arrow and ONLY, you must turn in that direction. A curved plus straight arrow lets you turn or go straight.
questions.manual_quote: a lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY, you must turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Your lane has both a curved arrow and a straight arrow. What may you do?
questions.answer: Turn in the arrow's direction or go straight
wrong: Only turn in the direction the curved arrow points
Only go straight
Only make a U-turn
questions.explanation: With both a curved and straight arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow or go straight.
questions.manual_quote: both a curved and a straight arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow or you may go straight.

questions.question: What does a white crossbuck with the letters RR painted on the pavement warn of?
questions.answer: A railroad crossing
wrong: A rest area ahead
A right lane ending
A road repair zone
questions.explanation: A white crossbuck and the letters RR painted on the pavement warn that a railroad crossing is ahead. They are used at many railroad crossings.
questions.manual_quote: A white crossbuck and the letters RR are painted on the pavement as a warning marker

questions.question: At night, when must your headlights be on?
questions.answer: From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
wrong: From sunset until sunrise
From 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise
From 15 minutes after sunset until 15 minutes before sunrise
questions.explanation: Tennessee law requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.manual_quote: Your car headlights must be turned on 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.question: During the day, you must turn on your headlights when daylight is not good enough to see people or vehicles clearly at what distance?
questions.answer: 200 feet ahead
wrong: 50 feet ahead
100 feet ahead
500 feet ahead
questions.explanation: If you cannot see people or vehicles clearly 200 feet ahead, your headlights must be on, even in daytime.
questions.manual_quote: you to see persons or vehicles clearly at a distance of 200 feet ahead

questions.question: It is raining hard enough that you must use your windshield wipers all the time. What does Tennessee law say about your headlights?
questions.answer: Your headlights must be on
wrong: Your headlights are optional in daylight
Only your parking lights must be on
Only your fog lights must be on
questions.explanation: Tennessee law says your headlights must be on whenever your windshield wipers are in use. It is not just a good idea.
questions.manual_quote: using headlights when wipers are in use is not just a good safety precaution — it’s Tennessee law!

questions.question: Your high beams are on. You must dim them when an oncoming vehicle is within how many feet?
questions.answer: 500 feet
wrong: 200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explanation: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet, about one city block.
questions.manual_quote: you must dim or lower the beam when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet

questions.question: Your high beams are on and you are following another vehicle. You must dim them when you are within how many feet of it?
questions.answer: 500 feet
wrong: 100 feet
250 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explanation: Dim high beams when following within 500 feet. The glare in the other driver's mirror can blind them.
questions.manual_quote: or when you are following another vehicle within 500 feet.

questions.question: Can you drive at night or in bad weather with only your parking lights on?
questions.answer: No, it is unsafe and against the law
wrong: Yes, if you drive below 35 mph
Yes, on well-lit city streets
Yes, if your fog lights are also turned on
questions.explanation: Parking lights alone are too small. Other drivers may think your car is farther away than it is.
questions.manual_quote: When there is limited visibility, the use of parking lights alone is not only unsafe, it is against the law.

questions.question: Why is driving with only parking lights on dangerous?
questions.answer: Other drivers may think you are farther away
wrong: Parking lights drain your car battery too fast
Parking lights can blind oncoming drivers
Parking lights can look like a turn signal
questions.explanation: The small size of parking lights fools other drivers about how far away you are.
questions.manual_quote: The small size of parking lights may cause other drivers to think your vehicle is farther away than it actually is.

questions.question: Your vehicle is stopped on the shoulder and visibility is limited. What lights does the law require?
questions.answer: Your parking lights must be on
wrong: No lights are needed, to save the battery
Only your fog lights must be on
Your high beam headlights must be on
questions.explanation: A vehicle stopped or parked on a road or shoulder in limited visibility must have its parking lights on.
questions.manual_quote: The law requires a vehicle stopped or parked on a road or shoulder to have parking lights on when limited visibility conditions exist.

questions.question: When is it illegal to use fog lights or other auxiliary lights?
questions.answer: When used alone, or when you must dim your high beams
wrong: Only during heavy rain, snow, or thick fog
Only on the interstate at speeds over 55 mph
Only inside the city limits between midnight and dawn
questions.explanation: Fog lights and auxiliary lights cannot be used alone or when you are required to dim high beams. Their glare blinds other drivers.
questions.manual_quote: It is also illegal to have auxiliary lights or fog lights on by themselves or on at times when you are required to dim

questions.question: What colors may steady-burning lights on the front of your vehicle be?
questions.answer: White or amber
wrong: White or blue
Amber or red
Any color you choose
questions.explanation: Since January 1, 2018, steady-burning front lights may only be white, amber, or white and amber (with exceptions for certain vehicles).
questions.manual_quote: steady-burning lights that display to the front of the vehicle in any color other than white or amber

questions.question: What flashing lights may a regular vehicle show to the front?
questions.answer: Only the emergency flashers put in at the factory
wrong: Flashing blue lights mounted on the front grille
Flashing amber lights of any kind
Flashing white strobe lights of any kind
questions.explanation: Since 2018, no flashing front lights are allowed except factory-installed emergency flashers (with exceptions for certain vehicles).
questions.manual_quote: any flashing lights in any color or combination of colors that display to the front of the vehicle, other than factory installed emergency flashers.

questions.question: A traffic officer tells you to drive through a red light. What should you do?
questions.answer: Obey the officer
wrong: Stop and wait for the green light
Honk and ask the officer to repeat
Turn right instead
questions.explanation: You must obey traffic officers at all times, even when they tell you to do something that would normally be a violation.
questions.manual_quote: You must obey traffic officers at all times.

questions.question: When going down a hill, may you coast with the transmission in neutral?
questions.answer: No, never coast in neutral
wrong: Yes, to save fuel
Yes, on short hills only
Yes, if you keep your foot on the brake
questions.explanation: Never coast in neutral on a downgrade. It reduces your control of the car.
questions.manual_quote: While traveling on a downgrade, NEVER coast with the transmission of the vehicle in neutral.

questions.question: In a manual transmission car going downhill, what must you NOT do?
questions.answer: Coast with the clutch pressed down
wrong: Use the foot brake to slow the car down
Shift to a lower gear early
Keep both hands on the wheel
questions.explanation: Do not coast with the clutch pressed down. Like coasting in neutral, it reduces your control of the car.
questions.manual_quote: drivers of manual transmission vehicles must not coast with the clutch depressed.

questions.question: You are behind a funeral procession on a two-lane road. May you pass it?
questions.answer: No, you may not pass it
wrong: Yes, if no cars are coming
Yes, if you use your flashers
Yes, after the first five cars
questions.explanation: Vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane road may not try to pass it.
questions.manual_quote: Vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway may not attempt to pass such procession

questions.question: When may you drive between vehicles in a funeral procession?
questions.answer: Only when a traffic officer directs you to
wrong: When there is a large gap between the cars ahead
When you have a green light ahead
When you need to turn right soon
questions.explanation: No driver may cut between vehicles in a funeral procession unless a traffic officer says to.
questions.manual_quote: No operator of a vehicle shall drive between vehicles in a properly identified funeral procession except when directed to do so by a traffic

questions.question: A truck is carrying a load that could blow off onto the highway. What does Tennessee law require?
questions.answer: The load must be enclosed or fully covered by a tarp
wrong: The truck must drive under 45 mph at all times
The truck must keep its hazard flashers turned on
The load must be tied down with at least one rope or strap
questions.explanation: Litter or loose material must be in an enclosed space or fully covered by a tarpaulin.
questions.manual_quote: to be in an enclosed space or fully covered by a tarpaulin.

questions.question: What is the range of fines for littering in Tennessee?
questions.answer: From $50 up to $3,000
wrong: From $10 up to $500
From $100 up to $1,000
From $25 up to $250
questions.explanation: Littering fines start at $50 and can go up to $3,000, based on the amount of litter.
questions.manual_quote: Littering is against state law. Fines start at $50 and can be up to $3,000 based upon the amount of litter.

questions.question: A person convicted of littering may have to spend up to how many hours of public service removing litter?
questions.answer: 40 hours
wrong: 8 hours
20 hours
100 hours
questions.explanation: You may have to spend up to 40 hours removing litter. The court may also order up to 8 more hours of work at a recycling center.
questions.manual_quote: A person convicted of littering is required to spend up to 40 hours of public service removing litter

questions.question: What does the Basic Speed Rule teach?
questions.answer: Drive at a speed that is safe for the conditions
wrong: Always drive at exactly the posted speed limit
Drive 5 mph under the posted limit
Drive as fast as the car ahead of you
questions.explanation: The Basic Speed Rule is a safety principle, not a law. It does not set an exact limit. The conditions decide what speed is safe.
questions.manual_quote: it teaches that the speed you may drive is limited by current conditions.

questions.question: The posted limit is 65 mph. It is night, raining, and you are on a two-lane highway. Is 65 mph a safe speed?
questions.answer: No, it is too fast for those conditions
wrong: Yes, it is the posted limit
Yes, if your headlights are on
Yes, if there is no other traffic
questions.explanation: The manual uses this exact example: 65 mph is too fast at night in rain or fog on a two-lane highway.
questions.manual_quote: 65 m.p.h. is too fast for those conditions.

questions.question: Under the Basic Speed Rule, your speed must let you stop within what?
questions.answer: The clear distance you can see ahead
wrong: A distance of 100 feet in front of your car
The next intersection
Two car lengths
questions.explanation: Adjust your speed to conditions so you can stop within the clear distance you can see ahead.
questions.manual_quote: Your speed must be adjusted to conditions so you can stop within a clear distance ahead.

questions.question: You are driving below the posted speed limit, but your speed is unsafe for the conditions. Are you breaking the basic rule?
questions.answer: Yes, even though you are below the posted limit
wrong: No, because you are under the posted limit
Only if you are driving on the interstate highway
Only if you cause a crash
questions.explanation: Driving at an unsafe speed for conditions violates the basic rule, even if you are slower than the posted limit.
questions.manual_quote: This applies even if you are driving slower than the posted speed or maximum limit.

questions.question: Under normal driving conditions, is it legal to drive slower than the posted minimum speed?
questions.answer: No, it is against the law
wrong: Yes, at any time
Yes, if you use your flashers
Yes, if you stay in the right lane
questions.explanation: Driving below a posted minimum is illegal under normal conditions. Bad weather, heavy traffic or a bad road are exceptions.
questions.manual_quote: It is against the law to drive slower than the posted minimum speed under normal driving conditions.

questions.question: When may you drive more slowly than the posted minimum speed?
questions.answer: In bad weather, in heavy traffic, or on a bad road
wrong: When you are a new driver or feel very nervous
When you are looking for an address on the road
When you want to save some fuel
questions.explanation: The manual allows slower speeds than the minimum only for bad weather, heavy traffic or a bad road.
questions.manual_quote: You may drive more slowly than the minimum speed if you are driving in bad weather, heavy traffic or on a bad road.

questions.question: There is no posted minimum speed. Can you still get in trouble for driving too slowly?
questions.answer: Yes, if you are so slow you block traffic
wrong: No, only speeding is against the law
No, unless you are on an interstate
Only if you are 20 mph or more under the limit
questions.explanation: Even with no posted minimum, driving so slowly that you block traffic is against the law.
questions.manual_quote: If there is no posted minimum speed, it is still against the law to drive so slowly that you block traffic.

questions.question: You are considered a slow-moving vehicle if you drive how far below the lawful maximum speed?
questions.answer: 10 mph or more below
wrong: 5 mph or more below
15 mph or more below
20 mph or more below
questions.explanation: Driving 10 mph or more below the lawful maximum makes you a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.manual_quote: if you are traveling at a rate of speed that is 10 miles per hour or more below the lawful maximum speed.

questions.question: You are driving slowly and a line of vehicles builds up behind you. At how many vehicles should you pull off when it is safe?
questions.answer: Five or more
wrong: Two or more
Three or more
Ten or more
questions.explanation: If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, turn or pull off the road as soon as you safely can.
questions.manual_quote: If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely.

questions.question: The car ahead stops suddenly and you cannot stop in time to avoid hitting it. What does this mean?
questions.answer: You were driving too fast or following too closely
wrong: The other driver is always the one who is at fault
You were fine as long as you were under the limit
Your brakes must have been broken
questions.explanation: If you cannot stop in time, you were either driving too fast for conditions or following too closely, even within the posted limit.
questions.manual_quote: you are either breaking the BSR - even if you were driving within the posted speed limit - or you are following too closely.

questions.question: Unless another speed is posted, what is the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways?
questions.answer: 55 mph
wrong: 45 mph
60 mph
65 mph
questions.explanation: Unless posted otherwise, the limit on these highways is 55 mph.
questions.manual_quote: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 m.p.h.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways?
questions.answer: 70 mph
wrong: 65 mph
75 mph
80 mph
questions.explanation: The interstate maximum is 70 mph. Drive that fast only in ideal conditions. Some sections have a lower posted limit.
questions.manual_quote: The maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways is 70 m.p.h.

questions.question: In crowded urban areas, what is the usual speed limit on Tennessee interstates?
questions.answer: 55 mph
wrong: 45 mph
65 mph
70 mph
questions.explanation: In crowded urban or metropolitan areas, Tennessee interstate limits are typically 55 mph.
questions.manual_quote: In the more congested urban or metropolitan areas of Tennessee interstates, the limit is typically 55 m.p.h.

questions.question: On an interstate, what is the slowest speed you may legally drive in the far left lane, unless heavy traffic keeps you from going that fast?
questions.answer: 55 mph
wrong: 45 mph
50 mph
65 mph
questions.explanation: Driving under 55 mph in the far left lane of an interstate is unlawful unless congestion prevents that speed.
questions.manual_quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle less than 55 m.p.h. in the left most lane of any Interstate highway

questions.question: What is the minimum speed in the right lane(s) of an interstate?
questions.answer: 45 mph
wrong: 35 mph
40 mph
55 mph
questions.explanation: The right-lane minimum on interstates is 45 mph under normal conditions.
questions.manual_quote: On the interstates, the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) is 45 m.p.h.

questions.question: The minimum posted speed on the interstate feels too fast for you. What should you do?
questions.answer: Use another road
wrong: Drive on the shoulder
Turn on your flashers and drive slower
Stay in the left lane
questions.explanation: If the minimum posted speed is too fast for you, the manual says to use another road.
questions.manual_quote: If the minimum posted speed limit is too fast for you, use another road.

questions.question: Most traffic is moving between 50 and 55 mph, within the speed limit. What speed makes you least likely to crash?
questions.answer: A speed within that 50 to 55 mph range
wrong: A speed well below 50 mph
A speed 10 mph faster than traffic
Whatever speed feels relaxing
questions.explanation: Flow with traffic that is within the limit. Slow drivers are as likely to crash as speeders.
questions.manual_quote: If most vehicles are traveling between 50 and 55 m.p.h., you are least likely to have an accident if you stay within that speed

questions.question: By law, what is going over the school zone speed limit considered to be?
questions.answer: Reckless driving
wrong: A warning only
A parking violation
Careless driving with no points
questions.explanation: By law, going over the school zone speed limit is reckless driving.
questions.manual_quote: Exceeding the school zone speed limit is by law considered to be reckless driving.

questions.question: How many points are added to your driving record for speeding in a school zone?
questions.answer: 6 points
wrong: 2 points
4 points
8 points
questions.explanation: The penalty is an automatic six points, which also triggers an advisory letter.
questions.manual_quote: The penalty includes an automatic six points added to your driving record

questions.question: When are school zone speed limits in effect?
questions.answer: When children are going to or from school, or at recess
wrong: Only from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on weekdays, all year
Only when a police officer is parked in the zone
All day and night, every day of the whole year
questions.explanation: School zone speed limits are in effect when children are going to or from school, or during a school recess.
questions.manual_quote: Speed limits in all school zones are regulated when children are going to or from the school or during a school recess hour.

questions.question: What color are the signs and devices that usually mark a highway work zone?
questions.answer: Orange or yellow-green
wrong: Blue or bright white
Brown or dark green
Red or pink
questions.explanation: Work zones are recognized by orange (or yellow-green) signs and devices, flashing lights, and workers in bright clothing.
questions.manual_quote: Highway work zones are easily recognized by the presence of orange (or yellow-green) signs and other orange traffic control devices

questions.question: What is the fine for breaking the posted speed limit in an active work zone?
questions.answer: At least $250 and up to $500
wrong: At least $50 and up to $100
At least $100 and up to $250
At least $500 and up to $1,000
questions.explanation: Tennessee law sets a minimum $250 and maximum $500 fine for speeding in active work zones.
questions.manual_quote: TENNESSEE LAW MANDATES A MINIMUM FINE OF $250 DOLLARS AND UP TO A MAXIMUM FINE OF $500 DOLLARS

questions.question: By law, how many separate ways of applying brakes must every automobile have?
questions.answer: Two
wrong: One
Three
Four
questions.explanation: All cars must have two braking methods, usually the foot brake and the parking (emergency) brake.
questions.manual_quote: By law, all automobiles must have two separate methods of applying brakes.

questions.question: What is the proper way to apply your brakes in normal driving?
questions.answer: Slowly and evenly, with gradual pressure
wrong: Quickly and hard, all at once
In short, sharp jabs, again and again
Only at the very last second
questions.explanation: Brake slowly and evenly. Braking too hard or fast can cause a skid and makes it harder for drivers behind you to stop.
questions.manual_quote: You should apply your brakes slowly and evenly by applying gradual pressure.

questions.question: Why should you start braking early?
questions.answer: It warns drivers behind you that you are slowing
wrong: It helps your tires last longer on the road
It keeps your engine from getting too hot
The law requires it before every single curve you take
questions.explanation: Braking early warns the cars behind you that you are slowing.
questions.manual_quote: Start braking early as a signal to the cars behind you.

questions.question: Your car does NOT have anti-lock brakes and starts to skid. What is the general rule?
questions.answer: Ease off the brake and steer in the direction of the skid
wrong: Press the brake pedal harder and steer away from the skid
Pump the brake and hold the wheel straight
Speed up and steer opposite the skid
questions.explanation: Without ABS, ease off the brake and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid, if you can do so safely.
questions.manual_quote: if the car starts to skid, take your foot off the brake and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid

questions.question: With anti-lock brakes (ABS), how should you press the brake pedal to stop?
questions.answer: Press down firmly and hold it without pumping
wrong: Pump it quickly several times
Light taps every second
Press it, then release, then press again
questions.explanation: With ABS, keep firm, steady pressure. Pumping the pedal disengages the anti-lock system.
questions.manual_quote: When slowing or stopping, apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal. Never pump the pedal with ABS.

questions.question: In an emergency stop with ABS, what should you do?
questions.answer: Press the brake firmly and steer around hazards
wrong: Take your foot off the brake and steer
Pump the brake quickly and hold the wheel straight
Pull the parking brake as hard as you can
questions.explanation: With ABS you "brake and steer": keep your foot on the pedal while steering around hazards.
questions.manual_quote: Always brake and steer when using anti-lock brakes

questions.question: You brake hard and feel noise and vibration in the brake pedal. Your car has ABS. What does this mean?
questions.answer: The ABS is working
wrong: The brakes are failing
You should take your foot off the brake
A tire has gone flat
questions.explanation: Noise and vibration in the pedal are normal and tell you the ABS is working.
questions.manual_quote: Expect noise and vibration in the brake pedal when your ABS is in use -- These sensations tell you ABS is working.

questions.question: What does "covering the brake" mean?
questions.answer: Holding your foot just over the brake
wrong: Resting your foot lightly on the brake
Pressing the brake and gas together
Keeping the parking brake half on
questions.explanation: Covering the brake means your foot hovers over the brake for a quicker response. It is a smart practice near hazards.
questions.manual_quote: "covering the brake" means the driver’s foot needs to hover over the brake or between the brake and gas pedals for quicker response time.

questions.question: Why is "riding the brake" (resting your foot on the brake) a bad habit?
questions.answer: It wears out brakes and makes others think you will stop
wrong: It makes your car speed up when going down hills
It turns off your brake lights and turn signals
It is only a problem when you are driving on the interstate
questions.explanation: Riding the brake adds wear and gives other drivers the false idea that you are about to stop.
questions.manual_quote: This adds much wear and tear on the vehicle’s brake system, and also gives other drivers the false impression that a stop is imminent.

questions.question: In a car with a standard (manual) transmission, how can you slow down for a stop sign?
questions.answer: Flash your brake lights first, then shift to a lower gear
wrong: Shift into neutral and coast up to the stop sign
Turn off the engine and let the car roll to a stop
Shift to a higher gear just before you reach the stop sign
questions.explanation: First flash your brake lights to warn cars behind you, then shift down.
questions.manual_quote: First, flash the brake lights to signal any cars behind you. Then, shift down to a lower gear.

questions.question: Most rear-end crashes are caused by drivers who are doing what?
questions.answer: Tailgating (following too closely)
wrong: Driving under the speed limit
Using their turn signals
Driving with headlights on
questions.explanation: Rear-end crashes are common, and most are caused by tailgating drivers.
questions.manual_quote: Rear-end crashes are very common and most of these crashes are caused by drivers who are "tailgating."

questions.question: To check your following distance, you watch the car ahead pass a fixed point, like a sign post. What do you do next?
questions.answer: Count seconds until you reach that spot
wrong: Count the cars between you and it
Measure the distance in car lengths instead
Check your speedometer and mirrors
questions.explanation: Count “one-thousand and one, one-thousand and two” until you reach the same point.
questions.manual_quote: count the seconds it takes you to reach the same spot.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the closest you should follow another vehicle?
questions.answer: No closer than two seconds
wrong: No closer than one second
No closer than one car length
No closer than five seconds
questions.explanation: If you reach the fixed point before counting to two seconds, slow down. Repeat until you are at least two seconds behind.
questions.manual_quote: Repeat this exercise until you are following no closer than two seconds.

questions.question: At what speeds does the two-second rule for following at a safe distance hold true?
questions.answer: At any speed
wrong: Only at speeds up to 30 mph
Only at speeds up to 55 mph
Only at speeds up to 45 mph
questions.explanation: The two-second rule works at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits. In bad weather, at night, and at higher interstate speeds, increase it to at least four seconds.
questions.manual_quote: This principle will hold true at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits.

questions.question: In bad weather, at night, at higher interstate speeds, or when following a motorcycle, what following distance should you use?
questions.answer: At least four seconds
wrong: At least one second
At least two seconds
At least three car lengths
questions.explanation: Increase from two seconds to a minimum of four seconds for better reaction time in these conditions.
questions.manual_quote: A minimum of four seconds should allow for better reaction time and a safer space cushion under these conditions including following a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is "perception time"?
questions.answer: The time it takes to see and recognize a danger
wrong: The time from seeing danger to pressing the brake
The time the car takes to stop
The time you wait at a stop sign
questions.explanation: Perception time is how long it takes you to see and recognize a dangerous situation.
questions.manual_quote: Perception time: The length of time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation.

questions.question: What is the average reaction time, from seeing danger to starting to brake?
questions.answer: About 2/3 of a second
wrong: About 1/10 of a second
About 2 seconds
About 3 seconds
questions.explanation: Reaction time is the time from perceiving danger to starting to brake. The average is about 2/3 of a second.
questions.manual_quote: Reaction time: The time from perception of danger to the start of braking. The average is 2/3 of a second

questions.question: What does your braking time depend on?
questions.answer: The type and condition of your brakes, and your speed
wrong: Only the color and size of your car
Only the time of day that you are driving
Only how many years you have been driving a car
questions.explanation: Braking time depends on the type and condition of your brakes and how fast you are going.
questions.manual_quote: Braking time: This depends on the type and condition of vehicle brakes, as well as vehicle speed.

questions.question: You are going 70 mph at night and a deer appears. Before you even start to brake, about how far will you travel?
questions.answer: 128 feet
wrong: 28 feet
60 feet
290 feet
questions.explanation: It takes 1.16 seconds to see the deer and move your foot to the brake. You cover 128 feet in that time.
questions.manual_quote: Before you even start to brake, you will have traveled 128 feet.

questions.question: In the manual's example of a car going 70 mph at night, what is the total stopping distance?
questions.answer: 418 feet
wrong: 128 feet
200 feet
290 feet
questions.explanation: 128 feet before braking plus 290 feet of braking equals 418 feet, about one and a half football fields.
questions.manual_quote: Your total stopping distance has now reached 418 feet

questions.question: According to the National Safety Council, about how far does a lightweight car going 50 mph need to stop?
questions.answer: About 200 feet
wrong: About 50 feet
About 100 feet
About 500 feet
questions.explanation: A lightweight passenger car at 50 mph can stop in about 200 feet.
questions.manual_quote: a lightweight passenger car traveling at 50 m.p.h. can stop in about 200 feet.

questions.question: How does Tennessee law define "stop"?
questions.answer: Your vehicle stops moving completely
wrong: Your vehicle slows to under 5 mph
Your vehicle slows until the way is clear
Your vehicle rolls slowly past the sign
questions.explanation: "Stop" means all movement completely ends. A rolling stop is not a stop.
questions.manual_quote: Tennessee Code defines "stop" as "complete cessation of movement."

questions.question: At a stop sign with a clearly marked stop line, where must you stop?
questions.answer: Behind the stop line
wrong: With your front wheels on the line
Past the line where you can see
At the edge of the cross street
questions.explanation: If there is a white stop line, you must stop your vehicle behind it.
questions.manual_quote: You must stop your vehicle behind this line.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no stop line and no crosswalk, where should you stop?
questions.answer: Where you can see cross traffic, before you enter the intersection
wrong: In the middle of the intersection, where you can see
Ten feet past the stop sign, just after the corner
Anywhere you like, as long as you slow down first
questions.explanation: With no line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest the crossing road where you can see traffic, and before entering the intersection.
questions.manual_quote: stop at a point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway

questions.question: There are no pavement markings at a stop sign. Where should the front of your vehicle be when you stop?
questions.answer: Even with the stop sign
wrong: Ten feet past the sign
Halfway into the intersection
One car length behind the sign
questions.explanation: If no markings are present, stop when the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign.
questions.manual_quote: stop when the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign’s placement on the roadside.

questions.question: A stop sign intersection has a marked crosswalk. Where must you stop?
questions.answer: Before the front of your car reaches the nearest crosswalk line
wrong: With your front bumper inside the crosswalk
On the far side of the crosswalk
Even with the stop sign, even if that puts you in the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Stop before the front of your vehicle reaches the nearest white line of the crosswalk.
questions.manual_quote: you must stop before the front of your vehicle reaches the nearest white line marking the border of the crosswalk.

questions.question: You stopped at the crosswalk but cannot see if cross traffic is clear. What should you do?
questions.answer: Edge forward slowly until you can see both ways
wrong: Go quickly before any cross traffic comes
Honk your horn twice and then drive right through
Back up a few feet to get a better view
questions.explanation: Once the crosswalk is clear, edge up slowly until traffic is clearly visible from both directions.
questions.manual_quote: If you cannot see whether the intersection is clear of crossing traffic, edge up slowly until traffic is clearly visible from both directions.

questions.question: You stop behind a car at an intersection. How much space should you leave?
questions.answer: Enough that you can see its back tires touching the pavement
wrong: About one foot, to save space
Close enough to almost touch bumpers
At least 50 feet back, which is about three car lengths
questions.explanation: A good rule is that you should be able to see the other car's license plate or its back tires where they meet the pavement.
questions.manual_quote: you should be able to see the license plate and/or the other vehicle’s back tire where it meets the pavement.

questions.question: The car ahead of you at a stop sign moves on. You move up to the stop line. What must you do there?
questions.answer: Come to a full stop again
wrong: Go through without stopping
Slow down and roll through
Honk and proceed
questions.explanation: Even after waiting behind another car, you still must come to a FULL STOP at the stop line.
questions.manual_quote: Remember, you still must bring your vehicle to a FULL STOP at the stop line.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
questions.answer: Stop completely, as at a stop sign
wrong: Slow down and go through with caution
Stop only if other cars are coming
Treat it the same as a green light
questions.explanation: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, just like a stop sign.
questions.manual_quote: A complete stop is required at a flashing red traffic light, just as with a stop sign.

questions.question: A flag person at a road construction site signals you to stop. What must you do?
questions.answer: Stop completely
wrong: Slow down and keep going
Stop only if workers are in the road
Go around the flag person
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when directed by a flag person or a police officer.
questions.manual_quote: You must stop completely when directed to stop by a flag person at a road construction site

questions.question: What is a rolling stop?
questions.answer: Slowing down without fully stopping
wrong: Stopping and then backing up a little
Stopping twice at the same stop sign
Stopping past the stop line by a foot
questions.explanation: A rolling stop is when you slow down but do not come to a full, complete stop. It is dangerous and illegal.
questions.manual_quote: A rolling stop occurs when the driver only slows down for a stop sign or traffic signal and proceeds

questions.question: What can happen if you make a rolling stop during your road test?
questions.answer: You can fail the road test
wrong: Nothing, if no cars are around
You only lose one point on the test
You must repeat that one turn
questions.explanation: Rolling stops are grounds for a traffic ticket AND for failing the driver road test.
questions.manual_quote: Rolling stops are grounds for receiving a traffic ticket AND for failing the driver examination road test.

questions.question: Which pavement markings are found at railroad crossings?
questions.answer: A large X, the letters RR, and a stop line
wrong: A yellow diamond, the word SLOW, and arrows
A white arrow, the word TRAIN, and a yield line
Blue stripes, the letters XR, and a dotted line
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings have a large crossbuck (X), the letters RR, a no-passing zone stripe and a stop line.
questions.manual_quote: Railroad crossings have pavement markings that include a large crossbuck ("X"), the letters "RR", a no-passing zone stripe and a stop line.

questions.question: As you approach a railroad crossing, how fast should you drive?
questions.answer: Slow enough to stop before the nearest rail
wrong: At the posted speed limit for that road
Fast enough to get across the tracks quickly
No faster than 45 mph in all cases
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that lets you stop before reaching the nearest rail.
questions.manual_quote: Every motor vehicle should be driven at a rate of speed that will permit the vehicle to be stopped before reaching the nearest rail

questions.question: A train is coming. How far from the railroad tracks must you stop?
questions.answer: Between 15 and 50 feet
wrong: Between 5 and 10 feet
Between 50 and 100 feet
At least 100 feet
questions.explanation: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the tracks. Never stop on the tracks.
questions.manual_quote: When you approach a railroad crossing and a train is coming, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks.

questions.question: Trains must sound their horn when they are about how far from a crossing?
questions.answer: 1,500 feet
wrong: 150 feet
500 feet
5,000 feet
questions.explanation: Trains are required to sound their horn about 1,500 feet before a crossing.
questions.manual_quote: Trains are required to signal a horn when they are approximately 1,500 feet from passing through a railroad crossing.

questions.question: What is the penalty for breaking the law at railroad signals or signs?
questions.answer: The same as violating other traffic control devices
wrong: Only a written warning the first time
Double the penalty of other violations
No penalty at all unless a train is actually present
questions.explanation: Railroad signal violations carry the same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices.
questions.manual_quote: Violations of railroad signals or signs carry the same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices.

questions.question: Must a school or church bus stop at a railroad crossing even when it has no passengers?
questions.answer: Yes, it must stop at every crossing
wrong: No, only when carrying children
No, only when signals are flashing
No, only at crossings without gates
questions.explanation: Church and school buses must stop before ANY railroad crossing, whether or not they carry passengers.
questions.manual_quote: Church or school buses, regardless of whether such buses are carrying any passengers at the time of crossing

questions.question: Which vehicle is required by law to stop at every railroad crossing?
questions.answer: A taxi carrying passengers for hire
wrong: A pickup truck carrying tools
A motorcycle with a passenger
A family car towing a trailer
questions.explanation: Common carriers, such as taxis or vehicles carrying passengers for hire, must stop at all crossings.
questions.manual_quote: Common carriers, such as taxis or other vehicles transporting passengers for hire

questions.question: Besides buses and vehicles carrying passengers for hire, which vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing?
questions.answer: Vehicles carrying flammable or explosive cargo
wrong: Delivery vans with empty cargo
Rental cars from out of state
Vehicles that have temporary paper license plates
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying flammables, explosives or other dangerous cargo must stop at all crossings.
questions.manual_quote: Vehicles transporting flammables, explosives or other dangerous articles as cargo or part of a cargo.

questions.question: How do tanker trucks usually warn you they will stop at a railroad crossing?
questions.answer: By turning on their emergency flashers
wrong: By honking their horn three times
By flashing their headlights on and off
By pulling over into the left lane
questions.explanation: Tanker trucks usually display emergency flashers before stopping at tracks. Buses pull to the right.
questions.manual_quote: will usually signal such a stop by displaying emergency flashers of the vehicle to alert other drivers to the impending stop.

questions.question: A school bus has yellow lights flashing. What does this mean?
questions.answer: The bus is about to stop, so slow down and get ready to stop
wrong: The bus is moving, so it is safe to pass it now
Children are getting on or off the bus right now
The bus has broken down and needs your help
questions.explanation: Yellow flashing lights mean the bus is about to stop to load or unload children.
questions.manual_quote: When the yellow lights on the front and back of the bus are flashing the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload

questions.question: A school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm out. When may you start driving again?
questions.answer: When the red lights stop, the stop arm goes in, and the bus starts moving
wrong: As soon as the children have reached the sidewalk safely
After you have waited 30 seconds and see no more children
When the bus driver honks the horn twice to signal you
questions.explanation: Wait until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving.
questions.manual_quote: Motorists must stop their cars and wait until the red flashing lights are turned off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins

questions.question: A school bus is stopped at an intersection loading children. Which drivers must stop?
questions.answer: Drivers from all directions
wrong: Only drivers behind the bus
Only drivers facing the bus
Only drivers turning right
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load or unload, drivers from ALL directions must stop.
questions.manual_quote: drivers from ALL directions are required to stop until the bus resumes motion

questions.question: What is the fine for not stopping for a stopped school bus?
wrong: From $50 to $100
From $100 to $250
questions.explanation: It is a Class A misdemeanor with a fine between $250 and $1,000.
questions.manual_quote: It is a Class A misdemeanor and the driver can be fined between $250 and $1,000 for not stopping for a stopped school bus.

questions.question: Besides school buses, the bus stop law also applies to which buses?
questions.answer: Church buses
wrong: City transit buses
Charter tour buses
Airport shuttles
questions.explanation: Drivers meeting or overtaking a school bus OR church bus with red lights flashing must stop.
questions.manual_quote: Any driver meeting a school bus or church bus on which the red stop warning signal lights are flashing

questions.question: You are on a highway divided by a median that cars cannot drive on. A school bus is stopped on the other side with its red lights flashing. What should you do?
questions.answer: You don't have to stop, but drive carefully
wrong: Stop until the bus starts moving again
Stop for 10 seconds, then go slowly
Speed up so you pass the bus quickly
questions.explanation: On a highway divided by a median or barrier that cars cannot drive on, drivers on the other side do not have to stop, but they must drive with caution.
questions.manual_quote: divided by median space or a barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic, the driver need not stop, but should proceed with caution.

questions.question: On a four-lane road with a center turn lane, a school bus stops with its red lights flashing. Who must stop?
questions.answer: Drivers in both directions
wrong: Only drivers behind the bus
Only drivers in the turn lane
Nobody, because the turn lane is a barrier
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is NOT a barrier. Drivers going both directions must stop.
questions.manual_quote: A turn lane in the middle of a four-lane highway is NOT considered a barrier

questions.question: Why must you never pass a stopped school bus on its right side?
questions.answer: That is where children get on and off
wrong: The bus driver cannot see the left side
The right lane is for buses only
Passing on the right blocks the bus mirror
questions.explanation: Never pass on the right side of a school bus. That is where children enter or exit.
questions.manual_quote: Never pass on the right side of the bus

questions.question: How do police vehicles signal you to stop?
questions.answer: With flashing blue lights, or blue and red lights
wrong: With flashing yellow lights and a short tap of the horn
With flashing green lights and a loudspeaker
With flashing white headlights and a bell
questions.explanation: Police use flashing blue or blue and red lights and/or an audible signal.
questions.manual_quote: by means of a visual, flashing blue or flashing blue and red lights, and/or an audible signal.

questions.question: A police car signals you to pull over. Where should you stop?
questions.answer: Near the right edge of the road, away from intersections
wrong: In the left lane, as close to the center line as you can
In the middle of the next intersection you reach
Right where you are, in your own travel lane

questions.answer: Either stay behind the car or go around it
wrong: Stay right next to the car and match its speed
Honk so the driver knows you are there
Flash your lights and stay beside it
questions.explanation: Driving where the other driver cannot see you is dangerous. Do not keep driving beside the car.
questions.manual_quote: Either stay behind or go around. Do NOT follow to the side.

questions.question: What is interstate hypnosis?
questions.answer: Feeling drowsy from steady road noise and little activity
wrong: Feeling dizzy from driving at high speed
Staring at another car's taillights at night
Feeling nervous and tense when you merge into fast traffic
questions.explanation: Steady sounds of wind, engine, and tires can make you drowsy. Keep shifting your eyes and take breaks.
questions.manual_quote: A condition of drowsiness or unawareness can be brought about by reduced activity and steady sounds of wind, engine, and tire hum.

questions.question: On a long interstate trip, how often should you stop and get out of the car?
questions.answer: At least every two hours, or about every 100 miles
wrong: At least every four hours, or about every 200 miles
At least every hour, or about every 50 miles
Only when you start to feel sleepy
questions.explanation: Stop even if you feel well. Walking around lets your muscles relax.
questions.manual_quote: Take a break and get out of the car at least every two hours, or every 100 miles or so.

questions.question: To be safest for you and others, what is the most hours you should drive in one day?
questions.answer: 8 hours
wrong: 6 hours
10 hours
12 hours
questions.explanation: It is safest for you and others if you do not drive more than eight hours per day.
questions.manual_quote: It is safest for you and others if you do not drive more than eight hours per day.

questions.question: On a 4-lane highway, you approach an emergency vehicle stopped on the shoulder with flashing lights. If it is safe, what must you do?
questions.answer: Change into a lane that is not next to it
wrong: Stay in your lane and keep going at the same speed
Stop in your lane behind it
Drive on the far shoulder to pass it
questions.explanation: This is the Move Over law. Leave the lane next to the stopped vehicle empty as a safety barrier.
questions.manual_quote: the motorist must yield the right-of-way by making a lane change into a lane that is NOT adjacent to the stationary emergency vehicle.

questions.question: Under the Move Over law, what do you do if changing lanes would be unsafe?
questions.answer: Slow down and go past with caution
wrong: Stop in your lane until it leaves
Speed up to get past it quickly
Honk to warn the people outside
questions.explanation: You may stay in your lane only when changing lanes is impossible or unsafe. Then you must slow down and pass with caution.
questions.manual_quote: If changing lanes would be impossible or unsafe, proceed with due caution, reduce the speed of the vehicle

questions.question: Which stopped vehicles with flashing lights does the Move Over law cover?
questions.answer: Emergency, utility, tow, and road work vehicles, and any car with flashers on
wrong: Only police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances that have their sirens on
Only fire trucks and ambulances that are stopped on the shoulder
Only vehicles that are stopped on the shoulder of the interstate
questions.explanation: It covers police, fire, ambulance, utility, sanitation, tow trucks, HELP trucks, road crews, and any stopped car with its flashers on.
questions.manual_quote: this law now applies to all stationary motor vehicles, such as your car or truck, with their emergency flasher lights on.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the LEFT shoulder with lights flashing. Where should you move?
questions.answer: Into the right lane, leaving the left lane empty
wrong: Into the left lane, next to the vehicle
Onto the right shoulder
Into the median
questions.explanation: The Move Over law works on either side. Leave the lane closest to the stopped vehicle empty.
questions.manual_quote: If the emergency vehicle is stopped on the left shoulder, the motorist merges into the right lane of traffic

questions.question: Your car has trouble on the interstate. What should you do first?
questions.answer: Move to the right shoulder and turn on your emergency flashers
wrong: Stop right where you are in your lane and turn on your flashers
Move to the left shoulder and turn off your lights
Keep driving slowly in the right lane
questions.explanation: Get off the road to the right shoulder or emergency stopping area as soon as you can, and warn other traffic.
questions.manual_quote: If you have vehicle trouble, move to the right shoulder or emergency stopping area as soon as you can. Turn on your emergency flashers

questions.question: Your car broke down and you need help. How can you signal for help?
questions.answer: Raise the hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or antenna
wrong: Raise the hood and tie a bright red cloth to the side mirror
Stand in the road and wave your arms
Leave your trunk open and your headlights on high
questions.explanation: A raised hood and white cloth show other drivers and officers that you need help.
questions.manual_quote: If you need help, raise your hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or radio antenna.

questions.question: After a breakdown on the interstate, where is it better to wait?
questions.answer: In or near your car, on the side away from traffic
wrong: Walking along the shoulder of the interstate to the next exit
Standing behind your car in the lane
Sitting on the median between the lanes
questions.explanation: Walking along the interstate is dangerous. An officer will stop to help if they are not on another call.
questions.manual_quote: If possible, it is better to stay in or near your vehicle on the side away from traffic. Walking along the interstate is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a yellow TDOT HELP truck operator at a crash scene?
questions.answer: Follow their instructions just as you would a police officer's
wrong: Ignore them, since they are not police
Only follow them if a police officer or trooper is there
Stop and ask for their badge first
questions.explanation: HELP operators are trained for incident scenes and can remove vehicles that block traffic.
questions.manual_quote: You should follow their instructions just as you would those of other police or traffic control personnel.

questions.question: You have a crash on the interstate. Your car still drives and no one is seriously hurt. What may you do?
questions.answer: Move the car to the emergency lane and wait for police
wrong: Leave the cars in the lane until police arrive
Drive on to the next exit and call the police from there
Trade information and leave the scene
questions.explanation: Tennessee's Move It for Safety law lets you clear the lanes. You still must not leave the scene.
questions.manual_quote: you may pull the vehicle(s) to the emergency lane and await the arrival of a trooper or police officer to the crash scene.

questions.question: What should you do at a crash scene where someone has died?
questions.answer: Never disturb the crash scene in any way
wrong: Move the cars out of the lanes right away
Move the victim to the shoulder
Clean up the broken glass and parts
questions.explanation: Also, never move a seriously injured victim unless emergency personnel tell you to.
questions.manual_quote: Never disturb a crash scene in any manner when a fatality is involved.

questions.question: What number can you dial on your cell phone, for free, to reach the Tennessee Highway Patrol?
questions.explanation: Use it for highway emergencies or to report a driver breaking the rules of the road.
questions.manual_quote: Dial: * T H P (*847) and you will be connected to the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatcher

questions.question: How does driving at night compare to driving in the daytime?
questions.answer: More dangerous, because your headlights limit how far you can see
wrong: Safer, because there is less traffic and there are fewer distractions
Safer, so you can increase your speed
Just as safe, as long as your lights are on
questions.explanation: Your range of visibility at night is limited by your headlights, so drive slower.
questions.manual_quote: considerably more hazardous and difficult than daytime driving because your range of visibility is limited by your headlights.

questions.question: Why should you use low beams, not high beams, in fog?
questions.answer: Low beams let you see better and help others see you
wrong: Low beams make your car harder for others to see
High beams drain the car battery in fog
High beams make the fog get thicker
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam light reflects back into your eyes. Low beams put the light on the road.
questions.manual_quote: In fog or mist, never put your headlights on high beam because the light will be reflected back into your eyes.

questions.question: What does continuous hard braking on ice and snow often do?
questions.answer: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control
wrong: Helps you stop faster on the ice
Keeps the brakes warm so they do not freeze up in the cold
Makes the tires grip the road better
questions.explanation: Keep a safe speed for icy conditions so you don't need hard braking.
questions.manual_quote: Continuous hard braking on snow and ice can result in the locking of the front brakes causing a loss of steering.

questions.question: By law, your headlights must let you see a person on the highway at least how far ahead?
questions.answer: 200 feet
wrong: 100 feet
350 feet
500 feet
questions.explanation: Headlights must be in good order, aimed correctly, and have clean lenses to meet this rule.
questions.manual_quote: see clearly any person on the highway at least two hundred (200) feet ahead of your car.

questions.question: What is the basic rule for safe night driving?
questions.answer: Never outrun your headlights
wrong: Always use your high beams
Follow the taillights of the car ahead
Drive at the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: Drive slow enough that you can stop within the distance your headlights let you see.
questions.manual_quote: The basic rule for safe night driving is this: NEVER OUTRUN YOUR HEADLIGHTS.

questions.question: What is glare recovery time?
questions.answer: The time your eyes need to readjust after bright headlights pass
wrong: The time it takes to dim your high beams
The time it takes your headlights to warm up
The time you need to bring the car to a stop after seeing a hazard
questions.explanation: During glare recovery you are almost driving blind. It is often worse for older drivers.
questions.manual_quote: it takes an interval of time for the pupil to readjust to the less intense light. This is called glare recovery time.

questions.question: An oncoming car's headlights are bright. Where should you look?
questions.answer: At the right edge of the road
wrong: Straight into the oncoming headlights
At the center line of the road
At your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Use the white line or road edge on the right as a steering guide until the car passes.
questions.manual_quote: Avoid the glare of oncoming lights by watching the right edge of the road

questions.question: Why should you avoid flashing your high beams to warn another driver?
questions.answer: It can distract them and cause a crash
wrong: It can burn out your headlight bulbs
It is the only way to signal a turn at night
It makes your battery run down quickly
questions.explanation: Flashing your high beams can interfere with the other driver's driving.
questions.manual_quote: Avoid flashing your high beams to warn the other driver as it might serve as a distraction and interfere with their driving

questions.question: At night, you must dim your high beams when meeting or overtaking a vehicle within how many feet?
questions.answer: 500 feet
wrong: 200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explanation: Dim your lights when meeting or overtaking vehicles within 500 feet.
questions.manual_quote: Meeting or overtaking vehicles within 500 feet.

questions.question: Which headlights should you use when driving at night in cities and towns?
questions.answer: Always use your low beams
wrong: Always use your high beams
Use high beams unless a car is in front of you
Use only your parking lights
questions.explanation: In cities and towns, always use your low beams.
questions.manual_quote: Driving in cities and towns always use your low beams

questions.question: You park on or along a highway at night. Which lights should you leave on?
questions.answer: Your emergency flashers and parking lights
wrong: Your headlights on high beam
