Your headlights on low beam
No lights at all
questions.explanation: Never leave your headlights on when parked. They can blind and confuse other drivers.
questions.manual_quote: Whenever you park on or along a highway at night, leave your emergency and parking lights on.

questions.question: To fight glare, how often should you clean your headlights and your windows, both inside and out?
questions.answer: At least once a month
wrong: At least once a year
At least every six months
Only when they look dirty
questions.explanation: Keep every surface between your eyes and the road clear, including both sides of the windshield and your glasses.
questions.manual_quote: Clean your headlights and the windows (inside and out) at least once a month.

questions.question: When is wet pavement especially slippery?
questions.answer: When it first begins to rain
wrong: After it has rained for an hour
Only when the rain turns to ice
Only on gravel roads
questions.explanation: Dirt and oil on the road mix with the first rain and make a greasy film.
questions.manual_quote: The pavement is particularly treacherous when it first begins to rain.

questions.question: When should you turn on your wipers after rain starts?
questions.answer: After a few seconds, once there is water on the glass
wrong: Before the rain starts, to dry the glass
Only after you can no longer see the road
After it has been raining steadily for about five minutes
questions.explanation: Wipers need enough water to clear the windshield instead of smearing dust and grime.
questions.manual_quote: wait a few seconds after rain starts before you turn them on.

questions.question: During the DAYTIME, you drive in dense fog, heavy rain, or snow. What does Tennessee law require?
questions.answer: Turn on your low beam headlights
wrong: Turn on your high beam headlights
Use only your parking lights
Use only your fog lights
questions.explanation: Low beams help you see and help others see you. Never drive with just parking or fog lights on.
questions.manual_quote: WHEN DRIVING THROUGH DENSE FOG, HEAVY RAIN OR SNOW DURING THE DAYTIME, TURN ON YOU LOW BEAM HEADLIGHTS.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog or smoke?
questions.answer: Don't drive in it
wrong: Drive faster to get through it quickly
Use high beams to see farther
Stay close behind another car's taillights
questions.explanation: If you must drive, use low beams, slow down, stay to the right, and avoid passing.
questions.manual_quote: The best advice for driving in fog or smoke is “DON’T”.

questions.question: In fog, you can no longer see the edge of the road. What should you do?
questions.answer: Pull well off the road to the right and turn on your flashers
wrong: Stop right where you are in your lane and turn on your flashers
Switch to high beams and keep going
Follow the center line until the fog clears
questions.explanation: Do not stop on the roadway unless you must. Get well out of the traffic lane.
questions.manual_quote: pull off as far to the right as possible – well out of the traffic lane – and turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.question: Why should you keep the radio off or low and not use a cell phone in fog?
questions.answer: So you can listen for other traffic
wrong: So your battery will not run down
Because radio signals are weak in fog
So your headlights stay bright
questions.explanation: In fog you may hear other traffic before you can see it.
questions.manual_quote: Listen for traffic (keep radio off or turned down low and do NOT use cell phone while driving in fog).

questions.question: On a cold day, which part of the road tends to freeze first?
questions.answer: Bridges and overpasses
wrong: Roads in direct sunlight
Long straight sections of highway
Roads next to open fields
questions.explanation: Shaded spots from trees or buildings also freeze first and dry out last.
questions.manual_quote: Bridges and overpasses can also hide spots of ice. They tend to freeze before the rest of the road does.

questions.question: On cold, wet days, where can spots of ice hide?
questions.answer: In shade from trees or buildings
wrong: On the sunny side of a hill
In the middle of busy intersections
On freshly paved roads only
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze first and dry out last.
questions.manual_quote: On cold, wet days, shade from trees or buildings can hide spots of ice. These areas freeze first and dry out last.

questions.question: When the temperature is close to freezing, how slippery may an icy road be?
questions.answer: It may be more slippery than at colder temperatures
wrong: It may be less slippery than at colder temperatures
It is completely safe to drive on
It is only slippery on bridges
questions.explanation: Ice near the freezing point can be even more slippery than ice at colder temperatures.
questions.manual_quote: Close to the freezing point, the road is icy and may be more slippery than at colder temperatures.

questions.question: Your car starts to hydroplane on a wet road. What should you do?
questions.answer: Slow down gradually by letting up on the gas
wrong: Slam on the brakes right away
Speed up a little so you can push through the water
Turn the wheel sharply to the side
questions.explanation: When hydroplaning, your tires lose the grip needed to steer and brake. Don't slam on the brakes.
questions.manual_quote: If you vehicle starts to hydroplane, slow down gradually by letting up on the gas.

questions.question: When a car hydroplanes, what may happen to its stopping distance?
questions.answer: It may triple
wrong: It may double
It may be cut in half
It stays the same
questions.explanation: Steering control may also be reduced or lost.
questions.manual_quote: Stopping distances may be tripled and steering control may be reduced or lost.

questions.question: At what speeds can hydroplaning happen?
questions.answer: At any speed, but it is more common at higher speeds
wrong: Only above 55 mph
Only above 70 mph
Only with worn-out tires
questions.explanation: This is one reason to be extremely careful in rainy weather.
questions.manual_quote: Hydroplaning is more common at higher speeds, although tires can hydroplane under certain conditions at ANY speed.

questions.question: What causes most skids?
questions.answer: Driving too fast for conditions
wrong: Driving too slowly in the rain
Using low beam headlights
Keeping too much following distance
questions.explanation: Skids happen when the tires can no longer grip the road.
questions.manual_quote: Skids are caused by drivers traveling too fast for conditions.

questions.question: Your car begins to skid. What should you do with the brake?
questions.answer: Stay off the brake until the car slows
wrong: Press the brake hard and hold it
Pump the brake quickly
Press the brake and the gas together
questions.explanation: Until the car slows, the brakes will not work and could make you skid more.
questions.manual_quote: Stay off the brake. Until the vehicle slows, your brakes will not work and could cause you to skid more.

questions.question: The rear of your car is skidding to the LEFT. Which way should you steer?
questions.answer: To the left, the way you want the car to go
wrong: To the right, away from the skid
Hold the wheel straight and brake hard
Turn the wheel all the way to the right
questions.explanation: Steer the way you want to go. As the car straightens, turn the wheel back so you don't start a new skid.
questions.manual_quote: If rear of vehicle is skidding to the left you want to steer to the left

questions.question: Your wheels go off the paved road onto the shoulder. What is the first thing to do?
questions.answer: Lift your foot off the gas, but do not brake suddenly
wrong: Brake hard to stop as fast as you can
Jerk the steering wheel quickly to get back onto the road
Speed up to get back on the pavement
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel firmly, brake lightly, and steer straight. Turn back onto the road only after you slow down and traffic is clear.
questions.manual_quote: Stop feeding the gas. Lift you foot off the gas pedal but do NOT suddenly apply the brake.

questions.question: After your wheels go off the pavement, when can you steer back onto the road?
questions.answer: After you slow down and nearby traffic is clear
wrong: Right away, before you lose speed
As soon as you feel the shoulder
Only after you come to a complete stop on the shoulder
questions.explanation: Do NOT steer back while there are cars near you. Slow down first.
questions.manual_quote: Once oncoming traffic is clear and you have slowed the speed of your vehicle you can turn back onto the pavement.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of rumble stripes on the edge line?
questions.answer: To make the edge line easier to see on wet nights
wrong: To slow cars down in school zones
To mark where you may pass
To keep water from freezing on the edge of the road
questions.explanation: The grooves let water drain off the line. The noise and vibration are a secondary effect.
questions.manual_quote: its primary function is to improve wet-night visibility of the edge line.

questions.question: What is the least amount of fast-moving flood water that can knock a person off their feet?
questions.answer: Six inches
wrong: Two feet
Three feet
Waist-deep water
questions.explanation: Most people do not realize how strong moving water is.
questions.manual_quote: only six inches of fast-movingflood water can knock a person off their feet.

questions.question: What is the least amount of moving water that can sweep most cars away?
questions.answer: 18 to 24 inches
wrong: 4 to 6 inches
36 to 48 inches
5 to 6 feet
questions.explanation: A heavy car does not keep you safe. Cars float, and trucks and SUVs have only 6 to 12 more inches of clearance.
questions.manual_quote: most cars can be swept away in 18 to 24 inches of moving water.

questions.question: What is the least amount of water that may cause you to lose control of your vehicle?
questions.answer: Six to twelve inches
wrong: One to two inches
Three to four feet
Five feet or more
questions.explanation: Two feet of water will carry most cars downstream. Never drive through floodwaters.
questions.manual_quote: As little as six to twelve inches of water may cause you to lose control of your vehicle

questions.question: You come to a road covered by flood water. What should you do?
questions.answer: Turn around and find another way
wrong: Drive through slowly in low gear
Drive through quickly to keep momentum
Follow another car through the water
questions.explanation: Do not drive into flood water. The water may be deeper than it looks, and the road under it may be washed out.
questions.manual_quote: TURN AROUND, DON’T DROWN®.

questions.question: Your car stalls in flood water. What should you do?
questions.answer: Leave it right away and go to higher ground
wrong: Stay inside and wait for the water to go down
Keep trying to restart the engine
Push the car to the other side
questions.explanation: Flooded roads can hide serious damage. Get out and get to higher ground.
questions.manual_quote: If your vehicle stalls, leave it immediately and seek higher ground.

questions.question: A driver knowingly ignores flood barricades and drives into a flooded road. What can happen?
questions.answer: They can be charged with reckless driving and made to pay for their rescue
wrong: Nothing happens to them, as long as nobody in the car is hurt
They get a warning only
They get one point on their record
questions.explanation: Respect "Road Closed" barriers. They warn you of danger.
questions.manual_quote: the driver can be charged with reckless driving.

questions.question: You spot a tornado while driving. What should you do?
questions.answer: Get out of the car and lie face down in a ditch or low area
wrong: Drive as fast as you can to try to outrun it
Stay inside the car and park under a tree
Park on top of a hill and wait in the car
questions.explanation: Do NOT try to outrun a tornado. Lying face down protects you from flying debris.
questions.manual_quote: DON’T try to outrun it. Get out of the car, find shelter in a ditch or low-lying area and lie face down

questions.question: How can you gain more control of your vehicle in a strong wind?
questions.answer: Slow down
wrong: Speed up
Drive on the shoulder
Follow a large truck closely
questions.explanation: Wind is especially dangerous for campers, trailers, and lightweight vehicles.
questions.manual_quote: To gain more control over vehicles in a strong wind, slow down.

questions.question: A truck or bus is passing you on the left. What should you do?
questions.answer: Move to the right side of your lane and slow down
wrong: Move to the left side of your lane and speed up a little
Brake hard and stop
Change lanes to the left
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create gusts of wind. Be ready to correct your steering.
questions.manual_quote: move as far as possible to the right of your lane and slow down.

questions.question: How does a strong tailwind (wind from behind) affect your driving?
questions.answer: It increases your speed, so you must brake earlier
wrong: It slows you down, so you must speed up
It makes steering much easier
It has no effect on stopping
questions.explanation: A headwind does the opposite: you may need more gas and steering is harder.
questions.manual_quote: will increase your speed, so you will have to decelerate and begin braking earlier to stop.

questions.question: Your car is stuck in mud or snow. What is the right way to get it free?
questions.answer: Use low gear and gently rock forward and back without spinning the wheels
wrong: Press the gas hard so the wheels spin fast
Put boards under the tires while they spin
Turn the front wheels hard to one side and press the gas to the floor
questions.explanation: Avoid spinning the wheels. Never put boards under the tires while they are spinning or the car is in gear.
questions.manual_quote: Repeat forward - backward rocking until the car rolls free.

questions.question: Which is one of the three big errors drivers make in snow and ice?
questions.answer: Over-braking and sliding the wheels
wrong: Driving with low beams on
Keeping a slow, steady speed
Clearing all windows before driving
questions.explanation: The three big errors are over-powering (spinning), over-braking (sliding), and over-steering (skidding).
questions.manual_quote: To over-brake and slide the wheels

questions.question: Before driving in winter, which windows must you clear of snow, ice, or frost?
questions.answer: ALL windows
wrong: Only the windshield
Only the windshield and driver's window
Only the front and rear windows
questions.explanation: Also clear headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and outside mirrors.
questions.manual_quote: Clear snow, ice or frost from ALL windows before driving.

questions.question: At 20 mph, low traction can increase your stopping distance to how many feet or more?
questions.answer: 200 feet
wrong: 50 feet
100 feet
500 feet
questions.explanation: Low traction makes stopping hard. Use brakes cautiously.
questions.manual_quote: When traveling at 20 M.P.H., low traction can increase stopping distance to 200 feet or more.

questions.question: How should you use antilock brakes (ABS) in an emergency stop?
questions.answer: Apply constant, firm pressure to the pedal
wrong: Pump the brake pedal quickly
Tap the pedal lightly over and over
Press, release, and press the pedal again slowly
questions.explanation: Push the pedal all the way to the floor if needed, even on wet or icy roads.
questions.manual_quote: To make antilock brakes work correctly, or work at all, you should apply constant, firm pressure to the pedal.

questions.question: Where should you go to find shelter in a hailstorm or sleet?
questions.answer: Drive under an overpass or bridge
wrong: Park under a large tree
Pull into an open field
Keep driving at normal speed
questions.explanation: In a hailstorm or sleet, find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge.
questions.manual_quote: Hailstorms/Sleet – find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge.

questions.question: The sun is behind you in the early morning. What should you be aware of?
questions.answer: Oncoming drivers may not see your car or turn signals
wrong: You will not be able to see the road
Your headlights will not work
Your car will look brighter and easier for everyone to see
questions.explanation: Driving toward the sun causes glare. Sunglasses, clean windows, and sun visors help.
questions.manual_quote: Be aware that they may not be able to see your turn signals or your car.

questions.question: What penalty does driving under the influence of drugs carry?
questions.answer: The same penalty as for alcohol
wrong: A lesser penalty than for alcohol
No penalty at all
A penalty only if the drug is illegal
questions.explanation: The penalties are the same for alcohol and drugs, even prescription or over-the-counter drugs.
questions.manual_quote: The penalties for a DUI arrest are the same whether the driver was drinking alcohol or taking drugs (even prescription or over-the-counter drugs).

questions.question: You had three beers in the past hour. About how long will it take for the alcohol to leave your blood?
questions.answer: About three hours
wrong: About one hour
About two hours
About thirty minutes
questions.explanation: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink.
questions.manual_quote: It takes about three hours to cancel the intoxicating effects of three drinks.

questions.question: As the percentage of alcohol in your blood (BAC) goes up, what do you become?
questions.answer: More intoxicated
wrong: More sober
More coordinated
More alert
questions.explanation: The higher the BAC, the more impaired you are.
questions.manual_quote: As the percentage of alcohol in your blood increases, you become more intoxicated.

questions.question: What does Tennessee's Implied Consent law mean?
questions.answer: By driving, you agree to be tested for alcohol or drugs if an officer asks
wrong: Traffic laws apply even without any signs, markings, or signals at an intersection
The owner of a vehicle will carry proper insurance
You agree to let police search your car any time
questions.explanation: The officer must have reasonable grounds to believe you are driving under the influence.
questions.manual_quote: when you drive in Tennessee, you have given your consent to be tested to determine the alcohol or drug content of your blood.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?
questions.answer: Alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination
wrong: Only reaction time
Only alertness and concentration, but not reaction time or coordination
None of them, if you feel fine
questions.explanation: Alcohol also affects judgment and vision, the two most important driving abilities.
questions.manual_quote: Drinking alcohol impairs a wide range of skills necessary for carrying out these tasks.

questions.question: How soon after a drink does alcohol start going into your bloodstream?
questions.answer: Within one to two minutes
wrong: Within 15 to 20 minutes
Within about one hour
Only after you finish eating
questions.explanation: Alcohol builds up in your blood as you drink.
questions.manual_quote: Alcohol begins to be absorbed into the bloodstream within one to two minutes after an alcoholic beverage is consumed.

questions.question: About how much alcohol can the liver get rid of (oxidize) per hour?
questions.answer: About one drink
wrong: About two drinks
About three drinks
About half a drink
questions.explanation: This rate cannot be sped up.
questions.manual_quote: the liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What is the only thing that can sober up a person who has been drinking?
questions.answer: Time
wrong: Drinking coffee
Taking a cold shower
Exercising
questions.explanation: Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not speed up how fast the liver removes alcohol.
questions.manual_quote: Only time can sober a person who’s been drinking.

questions.question: What is the lowest BAC that is always illegal for drivers 21 and older in Tennessee?
questions.answer: 0.08 percent
wrong: 0.10 percent
0.15 percent
0.20 percent
questions.explanation: Lower limits apply to drivers under 21. You can still get a DUI below 0.08 if you are impaired.
questions.manual_quote: In most states, including Tennessee, .08 is the level of intoxication which is always illegal.

questions.question: Which of these will affect you the most?
questions.answer: Three drinks in one hour
wrong: Three drinks in three hours
Three drinks with a large meal
Three drinks spread over a whole evening
questions.explanation: Spacing drinks over a longer time slows how fast you become intoxicated.
questions.manual_quote: Drinking three drinks in one hour will affect you more than drinking three drinks in three hours.

questions.question: You are smaller than your friends and try to drink as much as they do. What will probably happen?
questions.answer: Your judgment will be affected sooner
wrong: You will be affected later than them
You will be affected the same as them
You will not be affected at all
questions.explanation: The heavier the person, the more alcohol it takes to raise their BAC.
questions.manual_quote: try to drink as much as they do, your judgment and inhibitions will probably be affected sooner.

questions.question: Two people weigh the same and drink the same amount. Who will show signs of intoxication first?
questions.answer: The one with more body fat
wrong: The one with less body fat
The one who is taller
They will both show signs at the same time
questions.explanation: Alcohol is absorbed in water, not fat. People with less body fat have more water to dilute it.
questions.manual_quote: drink for drink, if people weigh the same, the one with more body fat will show signs of intoxication first.

questions.question: How does food in the stomach affect alcohol?
questions.answer: It slows absorption, but all the alcohol still reaches the blood
wrong: It keeps the alcohol out of the blood
It speeds up how fast all of the alcohol gets absorbed into the blood
It lets you drink more without any effect
questions.explanation: All alcohol you drink gets into the blood whether you have eaten or not.
questions.manual_quote: All the alcohol consumed eventually gets into the blood whether you have eaten or not.

questions.question: With a BAC of .10 percent, how much more likely are you to cause a crash than if you were sober?
questions.answer: Seven times more likely
wrong: Two times more likely
Three times more likely
Twelve times more likely
questions.explanation: At .15 the risk rises to 25 times, and at .17 to 50 times.
questions.manual_quote: With a BAC of .10 percent, you are seven times more likely to cause a crash than if you were sober.

questions.question: Small amounts of alcohol affect the two abilities that matter most for driving. What are they?
questions.answer: Judgment and vision
wrong: Hearing and smell
Strength and balance
Memory and speech
questions.explanation: Your ability to judge speed, time, and distance changes after only one drink.
questions.manual_quote: The two abilities most important to the driving task are judgment and vision, both of which are affected by small amounts of alcohol.

questions.question: Your ability to judge speed, time, and distance is changed after how many drinks?
questions.answer: Only one drink
wrong: Three drinks
Four drinks
Six drinks
questions.explanation: Each extra drink greatly affects your driving ability.
questions.manual_quote: Your ability to judge speed, time and distance are altered after only one drink.

questions.question: How much does alcohol reduce your ability to see clearly at night?
questions.answer: By more than half
wrong: By about 10 percent
By about 20 percent
It does not affect night vision
questions.explanation: Alcohol also slows glare recovery and reduces side vision.
questions.manual_quote: It reduces the ability to see clearly at night by more than half.

questions.question: At a BAC of .05 percent, side vision is reduced by about how much?
questions.answer: About 30 percent
wrong: About 5 percent
About 10 percent
About 75 percent
questions.explanation: Vision problems from alcohol greatly increase the chance of head-on or rear-end crashes.
questions.manual_quote: Side vision is reduced by about 30 percent at .05 percent BAC.

questions.question: Alcohol can impair your reaction time and coordination at a BAC as low as what?
questions.answer: .02 percent
wrong: .08 percent
.10 percent
.15 percent
questions.explanation: It takes longer to react, and coordination drops as you drink more.
questions.manual_quote: Reaction and coordination are impaired by alcohol consumption as low as .02 percent BAC.

questions.question: Is alcohol a stimulant or a depressant?
questions.answer: A depressant, in any amount
wrong: A stimulant, in any amount
A stimulant in small amounts only
Neither one
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows all nerve impulses and body functions. The "high" feeling comes from lower inhibitions.
questions.manual_quote: Alcohol, in any concentration, is a depressant, not a stimulant.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol is mixed with a tranquilizer or sedative?
questions.answer: The effects are multiplied
wrong: The effects cancel each other out
Only the alcohol has an effect
The drug makes you sober faster
questions.explanation: Even some over-the-counter medicines can affect driving.
questions.manual_quote: when alcohol is combined with another depressant, like tranquilizers or sedatives, the results are not just added together; they are multiplied.

questions.question: Your doctor prescribed a drug that impairs your driving. Can you still be charged with DUI?
questions.answer: Yes, a prescription is no defense
wrong: No, prescribed drugs are always legal to drive on
No, as long as you have the bottle with you
Only if you also drank alcohol
questions.explanation: Ask your doctor how a drug will affect your driving before you drive.
questions.manual_quote: Just because a drug is prescribed, by law, this is NO defense for driving under the influence of it.

questions.question: Can a driver with a BAC below .08, or even .00, be convicted of DUI?
questions.answer: Yes, if their driving is impaired by drugs or alcohol
wrong: No, a BAC under .08 is always legal
No, only a BAC test result of .08 or higher can prove a DUI
Only if they are under age 16
questions.explanation: A BAC below .08 does not clear a driver who is impaired.
questions.manual_quote: A driver can register a BAC of .00 percent and still be convicted of a DUI.

questions.question: Where does Tennessee's DUI law apply?
questions.answer: On public roads and in public places like shopping centers
wrong: Only on public highways and interstates, not other roads
Only on city streets
Only when driving over the speed limit
questions.explanation: The law also covers trailer parks and any place frequented by the public.
questions.manual_quote: or while on the premises of any shopping center, trailer park, apartment house complex, or any place frequented by the public

questions.question: You are arrested and refuse an officer's request to take an alcohol or drug test. What will likely happen?
questions.answer: The court will suspend your license for 12 months
wrong: The court will suspend your driving privileges for 30 days
You will get a warning only
Nothing, because the test is optional
questions.explanation: This is part of the Implied Consent law.
questions.manual_quote: it will likely result in the suspension by the court of your driving privileges for twelve (12) months.

questions.question: What does Tennessee's No Refusal law allow officers to do?
questions.answer: Get search warrants for blood samples from suspected impaired drivers
wrong: Arrest and jail any driver who has had even one drink, with no test needed
Take your car without a court order
Make you take a driving test on the spot
questions.explanation: The goal is to deter impaired driving and reduce crashes and deaths.
questions.manual_quote: allows law enforcement officials to seek search warrants for blood samples in cases involving suspected impaired drivers.

questions.question: What litter pickup must a person do after a DUI conviction?
questions.answer: Three 8-hour shifts while wearing an "I am a DRUNK DRIVER" vest
wrong: One 8-hour shift while wearing a reflective vest
Two 4-hour shifts with no special clothing
Ten 8-hour shifts while wearing an orange jumpsuit
questions.explanation: This applies to any DUI conviction, first or not.
questions.manual_quote: litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts. While removing litter, the offender has to wear a vest

questions.question: What is the minimum jail time for a first DUI conviction (BAC under 0.20)?
questions.answer: 48 hours
wrong: 12 hours
30 days
6 months
questions.explanation: If the BAC is 0.20 percent or more, the minimum is 7 days.
questions.manual_quote: 48 hours (7 days if BAC is 0.20% or more)

questions.question: How long is your license revoked for a first DUI conviction?
questions.answer: 1 year
wrong: 30 days
6 months
5 years
questions.explanation: A second conviction brings 2 years, and a third brings 3 to 10 years.
questions.manual_quote: 1st Conviction 48 hours (7 days if BAC is 0.20% or more) $350-$1500 1 year

questions.question: A driver commits DUI with a child under 18 in the car. What extra penalty is added?
questions.answer: At least 30 days in jail and at least a $1,000 fine
wrong: At least 2 days in jail and a $100 fine for each child
A warning letter to the parents
Ten extra hours of litter pickup
questions.explanation: These are added on top of all other DUI penalties.
questions.manual_quote: There is a mandatory minimum jail sentence of 30 days, and a mandatory minimum fine of $1,000.

questions.question: An impaired driver causes a crash that kills another person. What may they be charged with?
questions.answer: Vehicular homicide
wrong: Aggravated assault
Failure to yield
Careless driving
questions.explanation: If the crash injures someone, the charge may be aggravated assault.
questions.manual_quote: you are involved in a crash resulting in the death of another person(s), you may be charged with vehicular homicide.

questions.question: What does an ignition interlock device do?
questions.answer: Keeps the car from starting if the driver's BAC is too high
wrong: Locks the doors and slows the car down whenever it is speeding
Records how far the car is driven
Turns off the radio while driving
questions.explanation: Some DUI offenders may only drive a car that has one.
questions.manual_quote: ignition interlock device (which keeps a car from starting if the driver’s BAC is too high).

questions.question: What is the lowest BAC at which a driver age 16 to 20 can be convicted of underage driving while impaired?
questions.answer: 0.02 percent
wrong: 0.05 percent
0.08 percent
0.10 percent
questions.explanation: Being under the influence of alcohol or any other intoxicant also counts.
questions.manual_quote: at least 16, but is not yet 21 years old, and who is found: (1) driving with a BAC of .02 percent

questions.question: A driver under 21 is convicted of driving while impaired. What are the penalties?
questions.answer: They lose their license for one year and pay a $250 fine
wrong: They lose their license for 30 days and pay a $50 fine
They get a warning letter only
They lose their license for five years and pay a $5,000 fine
questions.explanation: The penalty sometimes includes public service work, too.
questions.manual_quote: Penalties for this conviction are: losing your license for one year, a fine of $250 and sometimes, includes public service work.

questions.question: You are 18, 19, or 20 and are convicted of buying or having alcohol. You were NOT driving. What happens?
questions.answer: You lose your driving privilege for one year
wrong: Nothing, because you were not driving
You lose your license for 30 days
You pay a fine but keep your license
questions.explanation: The law applies to any alcohol-related conviction, even if you were not in a vehicle. A second time means two years.
questions.manual_quote: The law applies to any alcohol-related conviction, whether or not you were driving or even in a vehicle.

questions.question: A person age 18 to 20 is convicted a SECOND time of buying or having alcohol. How long do they lose their license?
questions.answer: Two years
wrong: Six months
One year
Five years
questions.explanation: The first conviction brings a one-year loss.
questions.manual_quote: If it happens a second time you will lose your license for two years.

questions.question: A 15-year-old is found with alcohol. What happens to their driving privilege?
questions.answer: Suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer
wrong: Nothing happens to their driving, since they do not have a license yet
Suspended for 30 days
Suspended until age 16 only
questions.explanation: This applies to ages 13 to 17, even if they have never been licensed.
questions.manual_quote: your driving privilege will be suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer.

questions.question: How does the alcohol in a 12-ounce beer compare to a 1-ounce shot of whiskey?
questions.answer: It is about the same
wrong: The beer has much less
The beer has much more
The beer has none
questions.explanation: A 12-ounce beer has about as much alcohol as a 1-ounce shot of whiskey. Drinking beer instead of whiskey does not make you any safer.
questions.manual_quote: The amount of alcohol in one (12 ounce) bottle of beer is about equal to that in a (1 ounce) shot of whiskey.

questions.question: What is the first thing affected after drinking alcohol?
questions.answer: Your judgment
wrong: Your hearing
Your sense of smell
Your muscle strength
questions.explanation: That is why you should decide before drinking that you will not drive.
questions.manual_quote: The first thing affected after drinking alcohol is a person’s judgment.

questions.question: When is the best time to decide you will not drive after drinking?
questions.answer: Before you start drinking
wrong: After your first drink
After you feel the effects
When you are ready to leave
questions.explanation: After one or two drinks, alcohol affects your judgment and the decision gets harder.
questions.manual_quote: decide before you start drinking that you are not going to drive.

questions.question: What is a designated driver?
questions.answer: A friend who agrees ahead of time to stay strictly sober and drive
wrong: Whichever person in the group has had the fewest drinks by the end of the night
The oldest person in the group
Anyone with a valid driver license
questions.explanation: You can also give your keys to someone who is not drinking before you start.
questions.manual_quote: friends agree ahead of time which person will remain strictly sober.

questions.question: Why do young drivers have a much higher crash risk at a BAC between .01 and .08?
questions.answer: They have low tolerance for alcohol and limited driving experience
wrong: They usually drive newer cars
They have slower reflexes even when they are sober
They usually drive on interstates
questions.explanation: Most teenagers are intoxicated at low BAC levels.
questions.manual_quote: This is due to low tolerance of alcohol and limited driving experience.

questions.question: What should you know about over-the-counter cold tablets, cough syrups, and allergy medicine?
questions.answer: They can contain things that make driving dangerous, so read labels
wrong: They are always safe for driving, since no prescription is needed to buy them
They help you stay alert while driving
They only matter if mixed with coffee
questions.explanation: They may contain antihistamines, alcohol, or codeine. Watch for warnings like "may cause drowsiness."
questions.manual_quote: may contain antihistamines, alcohol, codeine and other compounds that can be especially dangerous for drivers. Read labels

questions.question: After a reportable crash, how long does the driver have to file a crash report with the Department of Safety?
questions.answer: 20 days
wrong: 10 days
48 hours
30 days
questions.explanation: This is required no matter who is to blame.
questions.manual_quote: must file an Owner/Driver Report of the crash to the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security within 20 days.

questions.question: You are not the first at a crash scene and your help is not needed. What should you do?
questions.answer: Slowly drive on and do not get in the way
wrong: Stop and look to satisfy your curiosity
Slow down to calm your nerves
Park nearby to watch the rescue
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at a crash (“accident gazing”) can cause more crashes and block emergency crews.
questions.manual_quote: slowly continue on in your vehicle so not to interfere with the arrival of police and emergency medical and fire/rescue services.

questions.question: Which of these can get a driver license revoked or suspended?
questions.answer: Fraudulently altering a driver license
wrong: Renewing your license a week early
Driving a borrowed car with permission
Moving to another county in Tennessee
questions.explanation: Frequent violations that add up to 12 or more points in 12 months can also lead to suspension for adults.
questions.manual_quote: Allowing unlawful use of a driver license, including fraudulently altering a driver license

questions.question: How do points work on your driving record?
questions.answer: Each traffic violation or crash on your record gets a point value
wrong: You earn points for each year of safe driving, which lowers your insurance
Points are given only for parking tickets
Points are given only when you renew your license
questions.explanation: Too many points can lead to losing your license.
questions.manual_quote: Each traffic violation or crash on a driver’s record is given a point value.

questions.question: An adult driver (18 or older) gets a notice of proposed suspension starting at how many points in 12 months?
questions.answer: 12 or more points
wrong: 6 or more points
8 or more points
15 or more points
questions.explanation: Adults with 6 to 11 points in 12 months get an advisory (warning) letter.
questions.manual_quote: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

questions.question: An adult driver gets an advisory (warning) letter for having how many points in 12 months?
questions.answer: 6 to 11 points
wrong: 1 to 5 points
3 to 8 points
12 to 15 points
questions.explanation: At 12 points, adults get a notice of proposed suspension.
questions.manual_quote: an advisory letter is mailed to any licensee having 6 to 11 points on his/her driving record within any 12 months.

questions.question: A driver under 18 gets a notice of proposed suspension starting at how many points in 12 months?
questions.answer: 6 or more points
wrong: 3 or more points
10 or more points
12 or more points
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 with 1 to 5 points get an advisory letter.
questions.manual_quote: Juvenile drivers (less than 18 years of age) who accumulate 6 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

questions.question: How often may a driver use the Defensive Driving Course to avoid or shorten a suspension?
questions.answer: Once in any five-year period
wrong: Once every year
Once every two years
Once every ten years
questions.explanation: The course can help avoid a suspension or shorten it.
questions.manual_quote: the Defensive Driving Course option is only available once in any five-year period.

questions.question: What happens if you drive while your license is suspended?
questions.answer: The suspension gets longer, and you could be prosecuted
wrong: Nothing happens, as long as you drive carefully and obey laws
Your suspension ends early
You only get a warning letter
questions.explanation: Never drive while your license is suspended.
questions.manual_quote: DRIVING WHILE YOUR LICENSE IS SUSPENDED WILL RESULT IN THE EXTENSION OF THE SUSPENSION PERIOD AND COULD ALSO RESULT IN CRIMINAL PROSECUTION.

questions.question: When your license is suspended or revoked, you must turn it in within how many days?
questions.answer: 20 days
wrong: 5 days
10 days
60 days
questions.explanation: Failing to turn it in means a $75 fine on top of other fines.
questions.manual_quote: it must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days of the suspension or revocation.

questions.question: If you move, you must report your new address to the Department of Safety within how many days?
questions.answer: 10 days
wrong: 30 days
60 days
90 days
questions.explanation: Without your correct address, you may miss important notices about your license.
questions.manual_quote: If you have a new address, you must report it to the Department of Safety within ten (10) days of the change.

questions.question: Which of these can make a person under 18 lose their driving privilege?
questions.answer: Dropping out of school
wrong: Getting a part-time job
Moving to a new school
Joining a sports team
questions.explanation: Failing to make satisfactory progress in school and carrying weapons on school property can also cause it.
questions.manual_quote: Dropping out of school (which is defined as having 10 consecutive or 15 total days in a semester of unexcused absences)

questions.question: For the under-18 driving rule, "dropping out of school" means how many unexcused absences in a semester?
questions.answer: 10 days in a row or 15 days total
wrong: 5 days in a row or 10 days total
3 days in a row or 5 days total
20 days in a row or 30 days total
questions.explanation: A student under 18 who drops out can lose the privilege to drive.
questions.manual_quote: 10 consecutive or 15 total days in a semester of unexcused absences

questions.question: For drivers under 18, what does "satisfactory progress in school" generally mean?
questions.answer: Passing three subjects per grading period
wrong: Passing one subject per grading period
Having a B average or better
Never missing a day of school
questions.explanation: Failing to make satisfactory progress can cost a minor their driving privilege.
questions.manual_quote: Failure to make satisfactory progress in school (which, in general, means passing three subjects per grading period)

questions.question: How many reckless driving violations within 12 months can lead to losing your license?
questions.answer: Two
wrong: Four
Five
Ten
questions.explanation: Drag racing and leaving the scene of an injury or fatal crash can also cost you your license.
questions.manual_quote: Two reckless driving violations within 12 months.

questions.question: Can driving away from a gas station without paying for fuel cost you your license?
questions.answer: Yes, your license may be revoked or suspended
wrong: No, it is only a store matter
No, it only adds one point
Only if you do it three times
questions.explanation: It is on the list of reasons a Tennessee license may be revoked or suspended.
questions.manual_quote: Driving a motor vehicle away from a gas station without paying for dispensed gas or diesel fuel.

questions.question: You get a ticket from another state and ignore it. What happens?
questions.answer: Your driving privileges will be suspended, revoked, or canceled
wrong: Nothing happens in Tennessee, since the ticket was from another state
Only the other state can punish you
You just get points added later
questions.explanation: Tennessee is in the Non-Resident Violator Compact. You must answer citations wherever you get them.
questions.manual_quote: If you ignore the citation — whether it was issued for a traffic violation here or in another member state

questions.question: How many points are given for speeding 46 mph or more over the speed limit?
questions.answer: 8 points
wrong: 3 points
4 points
6 points
questions.explanation: Points go up as speed goes up. For example, 1 to 5 mph over is 1 point.
questions.manual_quote: 46 m.p.h. and above in excess of speed zone

questions.question: When must you show evidence of financial responsibility (like proof of insurance)?
questions.answer: When you are charged with any violation or are in a crash
wrong: Only when the crash was your fault and someone was hurt
Only when you renew your license
Only when you buy a new car
questions.explanation: This applies no matter who was at fault. If you can't show it and are convicted, your license is suspended.
questions.manual_quote: This is required when charged with any violation or when involved in a motor vehicle crash without regard to apparent or actual fault.

questions.question: What does liability insurance cover?
questions.answer: Damages you cause to other people
wrong: Damage to your own vehicle
Damages uninsured drivers cause you
Your own medical bills only
questions.explanation: Collision insurance covers your own vehicle. Uninsured motorist insurance covers damage caused by uninsured drivers.
questions.manual_quote: Liability insurance provides coverage for damages you cause to other persons.

questions.question: Which insurance covers damage to your own vehicle, and is NOT required by Tennessee law?
questions.answer: Collision insurance
wrong: Liability insurance
Uninsured motorist insurance
Life insurance
questions.explanation: Collision insurance is not required, but you must still be able to show financial responsibility.
questions.manual_quote: Although collision insurance is not required by Tennessee law

questions.question: What does uninsured motorist insurance cover?
questions.answer: Damages caused by people who have no insurance
wrong: Damages you cause to other people
Damage to your car from weather
Your fines and court costs
questions.explanation: Liability insurance covers damage you cause to others. Collision insurance covers your own car. Uninsured motorist insurance covers damage caused by people who have no insurance.
questions.manual_quote: Uninsured motorist insurance provides for coverage for the damages uninsured persons cause.

questions.question: A driver loses consciousness because of a condition like epilepsy or diabetes. How long must they go without another lapse before they can get their license back?
questions.answer: At least six months
wrong: At least 30 days
At least three months
At least two years
questions.explanation: Their license must be suspended until then.
questions.manual_quote: must be suspended and remain lapse free for a minimum of six (6) months before being eligible for license reinstatement.

questions.question: You are involved in a crash. What does the law require first?
questions.answer: Stop right away at or near the scene, without blocking traffic
wrong: Drive to the nearest police station and report the crash in person
Keep driving if no one looks hurt
Stop only if the crash was your fault
questions.explanation: Turn off the ignition of a damaged car to prevent a fire. Never leave the scene.
questions.manual_quote: stop immediately at the scene, or as close to the scene as possible without obstructing traffic.

questions.question: Why should you turn off the ignition of a damaged vehicle after a crash?
questions.answer: To prevent a fire
wrong: To save gas
To lock the doors
To turn off the airbags
questions.explanation: If the car is on fire, help people out and move them away from it.
questions.manual_quote: Turn off the ignition in the damaged vehicle to prevent a fire.

questions.question: You must immediately notify police of a crash with death, injury, or property damage over what amount?
questions.explanation: In a city, call the local police. Otherwise, call the County Sheriff or the nearest Highway Patrol office.
questions.manual_quote: of any crash involving death, injury or property damage over fifty dollars ($50).

questions.question: A "reportable crash" must be reported to the Department of Safety. It involves death, injury, or property damage over what amount?
questions.explanation: The Owner/Driver Report must be filed within 20 days. Failing to report can suspend your license and registration.
questions.manual_quote: damage to the property of any one person, including oneself, is in excess of four hundred dollars ($400).

questions.question: When should you move an injured person out of a wrecked vehicle?
questions.answer: Only if you are trained or there is immediate danger like fire
wrong: Always, as soon as you arrive at the scene, so you can check them
Only if they ask you to
Only if the car is blocking traffic
questions.explanation: It is best to wait for emergency fire and rescue personnel.
questions.manual_quote: unless you have the necessary medical or rescue training or there is an immediate danger such as fire.

questions.question: After a crash, what information should you get from the other people involved?
questions.answer: Their names, addresses, license numbers, plate numbers, and insurance
wrong: Only the other driver's name and phone number, nothing else
Only the license plate number
Their Social Security numbers
questions.explanation: Also get the names and addresses of anyone hurt and of each witness. Then notify your insurance company.
questions.manual_quote: name, address and driver’s license number of other drivers; license plate numbers of other vehicles

questions.question: You arrive first at a crash scene. What should you do?
questions.answer: Call 911 to notify the police right away
wrong: Drive on without stopping
Move all the injured people to your car
Wait for someone else to call
questions.explanation: If you witnessed the crash, pull safely off the road, turn on your flashers, and tell the officer.
questions.manual_quote: If You Arrive First at a Crash Scene — Notify the police immediately by calling 911.

questions.question: You witnessed a crash happen. What should you do?
questions.answer: Pull off safely, turn on your flashers, and tell the police what you saw
wrong: Keep driving past the crash so that you do not get involved in it
Stop in the lane next to the crash
Take photos while driving past
questions.explanation: Police need witnesses. Pull off safely so you do not cause another crash.
questions.manual_quote: If you witnessed the crash occur, pull safely off to the side of the road and turn on your vehicle’s emergency flashers.

questions.question: What does "defensive driving" mean?
questions.answer: Staying aware, planning ahead, and expecting dangers to avoid a crash
wrong: Driving slower than all other traffic so nobody can hit you
Using your horn often so other drivers know you are there
Keeping your right of way so that other drivers always have to yield to you
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means staying aware, planning ahead, expecting dangers, and taking the right action to avoid hitting anything.
questions.manual_quote: “Defensive Driving” means being constantly aware of the driving conditions, planning ahead, anticipating dangers and taking the right action

questions.question: How far ahead do defensive drivers try to focus their eyes?
questions.answer: 10 to 15 seconds ahead, about 1 city block
wrong: 2 to 4 seconds ahead, about 2 car lengths
30 to 40 seconds ahead, about half a mile
5 seconds ahead, about the length of a driveway
questions.explanation: Looking 10 to 15 seconds ahead (about one city block) lets you see things early and gives you more time to react.
questions.manual_quote: Defensive drivers try to focus their eyes 10 to 15 seconds (about the distance of 1 city block) ahead.

questions.question: Which clues tell you a parked vehicle may pull into your path?
questions.answer: Exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights, and turned wheels
wrong: A clean windshield, a closed trunk, and a full gas tank
Open windows, a dim dome light, and a loud radio playing music
A parking ticket, a flat tire, and dirty headlights
questions.explanation: Exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights, and turned wheels are clues that a vehicle may move into your path.
questions.manual_quote: Look for exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights and turned wheels on vehicles.

questions.question: Before you drive through an intersection, in what order should you look?
questions.answer: Left, then right, then one more quick look left
wrong: Right, then left, then one more quick look right
Straight ahead only, since cross traffic must stop
Left, then straight ahead, then into the rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then take one more quick look left.
questions.manual_quote: look to the left first, since cars coming from the left will be closer to you. Then look to the right

questions.question: About how often should you check your rearview mirror?
questions.answer: About every 10 seconds
wrong: About every 2 minutes
Only when you change lanes
About once every mile
questions.explanation: Check the traffic behind you about every 10 seconds so you know if someone is moving up too fast or tailgating.
questions.manual_quote: Use your rearview mirror to check the traffic behind you frequently, about every 10 seconds.

questions.question: According to the defensive driving rules, what should you expect other drivers to do?
questions.answer: Expect them to do the wrong thing, and have a plan ready
wrong: Expect them to always follow the rules exactly
Expect them to yield to you because you have the right of way
Expect them to signal every time before they turn
questions.explanation: A defensive driver expects the other driver to make a mistake and has a plan ready to deal with it.
questions.manual_quote: Expect the other driver to do the WRONG thing, and have a plan of action prepared to counter his error.

questions.question: You are checking your following distance with the "1,001, 1,002" count. You reach the object before you finish saying "1,002." What should you do?
questions.answer: Slow down to make your following distance longer
wrong: Speed up and pass the car in front of you
Keep the same speed because the distance is fine
Flash your headlights at the driver in front of you
questions.explanation: If you reach the object before counting to 1,002, you are following too closely. Slow down to add space.
questions.manual_quote: if you reach that point before counting to 1,002 you are following too closely. If this is the case, slow down

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance to at least 3 to 4 seconds?
questions.answer: On fast interstates, behind trucks or buses, and in bad weather
wrong: Only when you are driving in a school zone during school hours, rain or shine
Only when you are driving on a dry road in the daytime
Only when the car behind you is following too closely
questions.explanation: Use at least 3 to 4 seconds of following distance on high-speed interstates, behind trucks or buses, and in bad weather or low visibility.
questions.manual_quote: when following large commercial trucks or buses, and in inclement weather or limited visibility conditions, it is safest to increase this following distance

questions.question: According to the manual, what are the most important driving attitudes you can develop?
questions.answer: Courtesy and consideration toward others
wrong: Speed and confidence in heavy traffic
Holding your ground when you have the right of way
Reaching your destination as quickly as possible
questions.explanation: Courtesy and consideration toward others are the key to safe driving.
questions.manual_quote: Courtesy and consideration toward others are the most important driving attitudes you can develop.

questions.question: Should you use your turn signal when you do not see any other vehicles on the road?
questions.answer: Yes, make it a habit to signal even when no one is around
wrong: No, signals are only needed when other cars are close by
No, signals are only needed at intersections with traffic lights
Only if a police officer or pedestrian is nearby
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals any time you change direction. Make it a habit even when you do not see other vehicles.
questions.manual_quote: Develop the habit of using your turn signals even when you do not see other vehicles on the road.

questions.question: You are driving between oncoming traffic and parked cars. The oncoming vehicle is a semi-truck. Where should you leave more room?
questions.answer: On the side the truck will pass on
wrong: On the side with the parked cars
Exactly equal space on both sides
No extra room is needed on either side
questions.explanation: "Split the difference" between two hazards, but leave more space on the more dangerous side. With a semi-truck, that is the truck's side.
questions.manual_quote: If the oncoming vehicle is a semi-truck, leave more room on the side that the truck will pass on

questions.question: You are coming up behind a bicyclist, and an oncoming car is approaching. What should you do?
questions.answer: Slow down, let the oncoming car pass, then move left to pass the bike
wrong: Speed up so you can pass the bicycle before the oncoming car arrives
Pass the bicycle and the oncoming car at the same time, staying in the middle
Honk your horn so the bicyclist moves off the road
questions.explanation: Take potential hazards one at a time. Let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then give room to the bicycle.
questions.manual_quote: if you are overtaking a bicyclist and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down, let the vehicle pass first

questions.question: What is the minimum gap you need when you change lanes, enter a roadway, or merge?
questions.answer: A four-second gap
wrong: A one-second gap
A two-second gap
A ten-second gap in traffic
questions.explanation: The manual says a minimum four-second gap is needed when you change lanes, enter a roadway, or merge.
questions.manual_quote: A minimum four-second gap is needed whenever you change lanes, enter a roadway or when your lane merges with another traffic lane.

questions.question: You need to cross several lanes of traffic. How should you do it?
questions.answer: Move over one lane at a time
wrong: Cut across all the lanes in one quick move
Cross all the lanes at once while using your hazard lights
Slow down to a stop and then cross all the lanes
questions.explanation: If you need to cross several lanes, take them one at a time. Never cut across multiple lanes.
questions.manual_quote: If you need to cross several lanes, take them one at a time. NEVER cut across multiple lanes

questions.question: When you cross or enter an intersection, what must you be sure of before you go?
questions.answer: That you can get all the way across without blocking it
wrong: That the car behind you has stopped completely
That you can make it halfway and wait in the middle lane
That your headlights are on low beam
questions.explanation: Do not block intersections. Make sure you have a big enough gap to get all the way across before you enter.
questions.manual_quote: DO NOT BLOCK INTERSECTIONS or get caught with a portion of your vehicle left in a traffic lane with approaching vehicles.

questions.question: At 55 mph, about how long does it take to pass one vehicle?
questions.answer: About 10 seconds
wrong: About 3 seconds
About 5 seconds
About 30 seconds
questions.explanation: At 55 mph you need about ten seconds to pass a single vehicle, so you need a ten-second gap in oncoming traffic.
questions.manual_quote: At 55 M.P.H. you will need about ten (10) seconds to complete the pass of a single vehicle.

questions.question: Does passing another vehicle allow you to go over the speed limit?
questions.answer: No, passing does not allow you to exceed the speed limit
wrong: Yes, you may go up to 10 mph over the limit while passing
Yes, as long as you finish the pass quickly
Yes, but only on a two-lane road
questions.explanation: Passing does NOT entitle you to exceed the speed limit. As a general rule, pass only one vehicle at a time.
questions.manual_quote: Remember passing does NOT entitle you to exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: After you pass a vehicle, when is it safest to return to the driving lane?
questions.answer: When you see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror
wrong: As soon as your front bumper is past the other car's front bumper
When the other driver waves you over with a hand signal
As soon as you are side by side with the other vehicle
questions.explanation: Do not count on other drivers to make room. Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror.
questions.manual_quote: until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you just passed in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: Someone is tailgating you, and there is a lane to your right. What should you do?
questions.answer: Move over to the right lane
wrong: Tap your brakes hard to warn them
Speed up to get away from them
Stay in your lane and slow down quickly
questions.explanation: If there is a right lane, move over to the right. If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and passing is legal, then slowly reduce speed.
questions.manual_quote: If there is a right lane, move over to the right.

questions.question: Someone is tailgating you on a road with no right lane. What should you do?
questions.answer: Wait until passing is legal and the road is clear, then slowly reduce speed
wrong: Slow down quickly so the tailgater has to back off
Speed up until the tailgater falls far behind you
Stop in your lane and wait there until the tailgater finally goes around you
questions.explanation: Slowly reducing your speed encourages the tailgater to drive around you. Never slow down quickly, because that raises your risk of being hit from behind.
questions.manual_quote: If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and passing is legal, then slowly reduce your speed.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, how should you position your car when meeting oncoming vehicles?
questions.answer: Stay slightly to the right of your lane
wrong: Stay slightly to the left, near the centerline
Drive on the right shoulder until they pass
Drive right on top of the centerline
questions.explanation: When meeting oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road, stay slightly right so you do not crowd the centerline.
questions.manual_quote: When meeting oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road stay slightly to the right of your lane so as not to “crowd” the centerline.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space in front of your car?
questions.answer: Near railroad crossings, and when stopped on a hill or curve
wrong: Only when the road is dry, the weather is clear, and traffic is light
Only when you are driving on a one-way street
Only when you are about to park at the curb
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when you come up to a railroad crossing, or when you are stopped behind another vehicle on a hill or curve.
questions.manual_quote: Also leave extra space when approaching railroad crossings or when stopped behind another vehicle on a hill or curve.

questions.question: Another driver is following you after a road rage incident. What should you do?
questions.answer: Drive to a police station or a public place to get help
wrong: Drive home quickly, go inside, and lock the door
Pull over on the shoulder and talk to the driver calmly
Speed up and try to lose the driver in traffic
questions.explanation: If a driver follows you, go to a police station or public place. If harassed, get the tag number and report it.
questions.manual_quote: If a driver follows you, go to a police station or a public place where you can get help.

questions.question: Another driver is angry and honking at you. What is the safe response?
questions.answer: Do not join in, and give the driver plenty of space
wrong: Honk back so the driver knows you are upset too
Slow down in front of the driver to teach them a lesson about honking
Make eye contact and glare until the driver stops
questions.explanation: Don't join in the confrontation, even just honking or glaring. Give an angry driver plenty of space.
questions.manual_quote: Don’t join in the confrontation, even if it is just honking or glaring.

questions.question: According to the manual, in what kind of weather do most accidents happen?
questions.answer: In clear weather
wrong: In snow
In heavy rain
In fog
questions.explanation: Most accidents happen in clear weather. Pretty days can be deadly too.
questions.manual_quote: If you picked anything but (a), you’re wrong – pretty days can be deadly too!

questions.question: When a collision may happen, what three options do drivers have?
questions.answer: Stop, turn, or speed up
wrong: Stop, honk, or flash your lights
Turn, back up, or honk
Speed up, honk, or close your eyes
questions.explanation: To avoid a collision, drivers have three options: stop, turn, or speed up.
questions.manual_quote: In avoiding a collision, drivers have three options: 1. Stop 2. Turn 3. Speed Up

questions.question: Your car has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and you need to stop quickly. What should you do?
questions.answer: Press the brake as hard as you can and keep pressing
wrong: Pump the brake pedal quickly on and off
Press the brake gently, and let up as soon as the pedal starts to vibrate
Use the parking brake instead of the brake pedal
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake as hard as you can and keep pressing. You may feel the pedal push back. Do NOT let up.
questions.manual_quote: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it firmly.

questions.question: You are braking hard in a car with ABS, and you feel the brake pedal pushing back. What should you do?
questions.answer: Keep the brake pedal pushed down firmly
wrong: Let up on the brake pedal right away
Pump the brake pedal faster
Shift into neutral and let up on the brake
questions.explanation: Pushing back means the ABS is working. Do NOT let up. ABS only works with the pedal pushed down firmly.
questions.manual_quote: You might feel the brake pedal pushing back when the ABS is working. Do NOT let up on the brake pedal.

questions.question: Your car does NOT have ABS. You must stop quickly. How should you brake?
questions.answer: Brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels
wrong: Press as hard as you can and hold the pedal down even if you skid
Brake very lightly and let the car coast to a stop
Pull the parking brake as hard as you can
questions.explanation: Without ABS, apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking them. Braking too hard can cause a skid.
questions.manual_quote: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking them.

questions.question: In a car without ABS, your brakes lock and the car starts to skid. What should you do?
questions.answer: Quickly let up on the brake, then brake again once the skid stops
wrong: Hold the brake pedal down even harder until the car stops completely
Turn the steering wheel sharply back and forth
Press the gas pedal to get out of the skid
questions.explanation: If the brakes lock, quickly let up on the brake pedal. As soon as the skid stops, push down on the brake again.
questions.manual_quote: If the brakes lock-up, you will feel the vehicle start to skid. Quickly let up on the brake pedal.

questions.question: In most cases, which can you do faster to avoid a collision?
questions.answer: Turn the vehicle
wrong: Stop the vehicle
Back up the vehicle
Shift to a lower gear
questions.explanation: In most cases you can turn quicker than you can stop. If you can't stop in time, try to steer around the object.
questions.manual_quote: In most cases, you can turn the vehicle quicker than you can stop it.

questions.question: Where is it best to place your hands on the steering wheel?
questions.answer: At about the 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions
wrong: At about the 12 o'clock position with one hand
At about the 6 o'clock position with both hands
At about the 11 o'clock and 1 o'clock positions
questions.explanation: Hands at about 9 and 3 o'clock help you turn quickly and keep your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's path.
questions.manual_quote: It is best to have your hands at about the 3 o’clock and 9 o’clock positions.

questions.question: Why does the manual recommend the 9 and 3 o'clock hand positions?
questions.answer: They keep your wrists and arms out of the air bag's path
wrong: They let you steer with just one hand more easily
They let you rest your arms on the door and the center console
They make it easier to reach the radio and turn signal
questions.explanation: This hand position keeps your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's main impact area in a collision.
questions.manual_quote: This will keep your wrists and forearms out of the main impact area of the air bag located in the steering wheel

questions.question: After you steer away from a hazard, which way should you steer?
questions.answer: In the direction you want the vehicle to go
wrong: Toward the hazard so you can keep watching it
Toward the shoulder no matter what
Wherever the car naturally pulls
questions.explanation: Some drivers steer away from one collision only to end up in another. Always steer where you want the vehicle to go.
questions.manual_quote: Always steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.

questions.question: In a car with ABS, can you turn while you are braking?
questions.answer: Yes, ABS lets you turn while braking without skidding
wrong: No, you must let go of the brake before you turn
No, turning while braking will always lock all four of the wheels
Only if you pump the brake pedal while turning
questions.explanation: With ABS, you can turn the vehicle while braking without skidding. This helps when you must swerve and slow down.
questions.manual_quote: One aspect of having ABS, is that you can turn your vehicle while braking without skidding.

questions.question: In a car WITHOUT ABS, how do you turn quickly while braking?
questions.answer: Let up on the brake pedal, then turn the steering wheel
wrong: Keep the brake pressed hard and turn sharply
Pump the brake and turn the steering wheel hard at the same time
Press the gas, then turn the steering wheel
questions.explanation: Without ABS, you need to let up on the brake pedal first, and then turn the steering wheel.
questions.manual_quote: As you are braking you will need to let up on the brake pedal and then turn the steering wheel.

questions.question: When might speeding up be the best way to avoid a collision?
questions.answer: When a car is about to hit you from the side or behind, and there is room ahead
wrong: When the car ahead of you stops suddenly and there is no room to steer around it
When you are coming up on a stopped school bus
When a deer runs onto the road in front of you
questions.explanation: Speed up when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room in front. Slow down after the danger passes.
questions.manual_quote: This may happen when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or from behind and there is room to the front

questions.question: Which is generally better: turning off the road or crashing head-on into another vehicle?
questions.answer: Turning off the road
wrong: Crashing head-on into the other vehicle
It depends only on which vehicle is bigger
They are equally dangerous
questions.explanation: The manual says it is generally better to turn off the road than to crash head-on into another vehicle.
questions.manual_quote: generally it is better to turn off the road than to crash head-on into another vehicle.

questions.question: What time of year is the peak season for deer-car crashes?
questions.answer: Fall
wrong: Spring
Summer
Winter
questions.explanation: Fall is the peak season because it is mating and hunting season, so deer are more active.
questions.manual_quote: Fall is the peak season for deer-car crashes.

questions.question: At what times of day should you be especially alert for deer?
questions.answer: At dusk and dawn
wrong: At noon and midafternoon
Only at midnight
Only during morning rush hour
questions.explanation: Deer go out to feed at dusk and dawn. Scan the roadsides for your headlights reflecting in their eyes.
questions.manual_quote: Be particularly alert at dusk and dawn, when these animals venture out to feed.

questions.question: You see one deer near the road. What should you expect?
questions.answer: There may be several more deer nearby
wrong: The deer will stay put until you pass
Deer always travel alone
The deer will run away from your headlights
questions.explanation: If you see one deer, there may be several others nearby, especially near woods and water.
questions.manual_quote: If you see one deer, there may be several others nearby.

questions.question: At night, how can you help avoid hitting a deer?
questions.answer: Use high beams when you can to light the road's edges
wrong: Turn off your headlights so the deer are not scared
Use only your parking lights
Flash your headlights over and over to scare deer away
questions.explanation: Use high beams when possible to light the road edges. Flashing headlights may cause a deer to freeze in the road.
questions.manual_quote: At night, use your high-beam lights if possible to illuminate the road’s edges.

questions.question: You are about to hit a deer and a collision cannot be avoided. What should you do?
questions.answer: Do not swerve, and stay in control on the road
wrong: Swerve hard into the other lane to miss it
Swerve off the road onto the shoulder
Let go of the steering wheel and brace yourself for the hit
questions.explanation: If a collision seems certain, don't swerve. Your risk of injury may be greater if you do. Stay in control on the road.
questions.manual_quote: If a collision seems inevitable, don’t swerve to avoid the animal; your risk of personal injury may be greater if you do.

questions.question: You hit a deer with your car. What should you do?
questions.answer: Report the crash to the police
wrong: Leave, since animal crashes never need to be reported
Report it only if your airbag opened
Call your insurance company only
questions.explanation: Report the crash to the police if it involves a large animal such as a deer or a farm animal.
questions.manual_quote: Report the crash to the police if it involves a large animal such as a deer or farm animal.

questions.question: In a car with ABS, should you pump the brakes in an emergency?
questions.answer: No, never pump the brakes in a car with ABS
wrong: Yes, pump the brakes quickly to avoid skidding
Yes, pump the brakes if the pedal starts to pulsate
Yes, but only on wet or icy roads
questions.explanation: Never pump ABS brakes, even if the pedal pulsates. The ABS is already pumping the brakes for you, much faster.
questions.manual_quote: Never pump the brake pedal of a vehicle equipped with ABS, even if the brake pedal is pulsating.

questions.question: Is it safe to drive an ABS-equipped car more aggressively than a car without ABS?
questions.answer: No, never drive more aggressively just because you have ABS
wrong: Yes, ABS lets you take curves faster than usual
Yes, ABS makes sudden lane changes safe to do
Yes, but only when the roads are dry and there is little traffic
questions.explanation: Never drive an ABS car more aggressively. Fast curves and abrupt lane changes are not safe in any vehicle.
questions.manual_quote: Never drive an ABS-equipped vehicle more aggressively than vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What are the three major parts of the highway transportation system?
questions.answer: The driver, the vehicle, and the road
wrong: The driver, the police, and the weather
The vehicle, the fuel, and the tires
The road, the signs, and the speed limit
questions.explanation: The three major parts are the driver, the vehicle, and the road. Not paying attention to any of these three contributes to most accidents.
questions.manual_quote: Neglect or inattention to of any one or more of these three will contribute to most accidents.

questions.question: What is the single most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.answer: Human error
wrong: Bad weather
Mechanical failure
Poor road design
questions.explanation: Human error is the single most common cause. Leading factors are excessive speed, lack of concentration, and improper evasive action.
questions.manual_quote: Human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the leading factors in crashes, according to the manual?
questions.answer: Excessive speed
wrong: Driving with the windows down
Driving with the radio off
Driving a car that is more than 10 years old
questions.explanation: The leading factors in crashes are excessive speed, lack of concentration, and improper evasive action.
questions.manual_quote: The leading factors in crashes are: • Excessive Speed • Lack of Concentration • Improper Evasive Action

questions.question: How often should you have your eyes checked by an eye specialist?
questions.answer: Every year or two
wrong: Every five years
Only when you renew your license
Only if you have a crash
questions.explanation: Because seeing well is so important, have your eyes checked every year or two.
questions.manual_quote: you should have your eyes checked every year or two by an eye specialist.

questions.question: Your driver license shows Restriction Code 01. What does that mean?
questions.answer: You must wear corrective lenses at all times when driving
wrong: You may drive only during daylight hours
You may not drive on interstate highways or at night at any time
You must have an adult with you whenever you drive
questions.explanation: Restriction Code 01 means you must wear glasses or contacts whenever you drive. You can be ticketed without them.
questions.manual_quote: If your driver license indicates you must wear corrective lenses (Restriction Code 01) you must wear them at all times when driving.

questions.question: Why should you avoid dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night?
questions.answer: They cut down the light you need to see clearly
wrong: They make oncoming headlights brighter
They are illegal to wear in any vehicle
They make your eyes tired, but only if you also wear them in the daytime
questions.explanation: Dark sunglasses or tinted contacts cut down the light you need to see clearly at night.
questions.manual_quote: Avoid using dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night, they cut down the light you need to see clearly.

questions.question: In Tennessee, a person with epilepsy may drive if under a doctor's care and seizure free for at least how long?
questions.answer: Six months
wrong: One month
Three months
Two years
questions.explanation: In Tennessee you may drive if you are under a doctor's care and have been seizure free for at least six months.
questions.manual_quote: you may drive if you are under the care of a doctor and have been seizure free for a minimum of six months.

questions.question: On a long trip, how often should you stop and take a break to avoid fatigue?
questions.answer: Every hour, or more often if needed
wrong: Every four hours
Only when you need to stop for gas
Every 300 miles
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour or more often. Walk around and get fresh air. A few minutes can save your life.
