questions.manual_quote: Take breaks. Stop every hour or more often if needed.

questions.question: You are getting sleepy while driving. What does the manual say to do?
questions.answer: Stop and sleep for a few hours
wrong: Open the window and keep driving
Turn the radio up loud and keep going
Drive faster so you get there sooner
questions.explanation: Never drive if you are sleepy. It is better to stop and sleep for a few hours than to try to stay awake.
questions.manual_quote: It is better to stop and sleep for a few hours than to take a chance on trying to stay awake.

questions.question: When should you have a mechanic check your brakes?
questions.answer: When they are noisy, smell funny, or the pedal goes to the floor
wrong: Only when the car is due for an oil change
Only after the brakes stop working completely and the car will not stop
Only when the brake pedal feels firm and high
questions.explanation: If the brakes don't seem to work well, make a lot of noise, smell funny, or the pedal goes to the floor, have them checked.
questions.manual_quote: are making a lot of noise, smell funny or the brake pedal goes to the floor, have a mechanic check them.

questions.question: How should you check that your turn signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights work?
questions.answer: Check them from the outside of the vehicle
wrong: Check the dashboard lights only
Wait for another driver to tell you
Check them only during your yearly inspection
questions.explanation: Lights should be checked from the outside of the vehicle to be sure they work.
questions.manual_quote: These should be checked from the outside of the vehicle.

questions.question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
questions.answer: Longer stopping distance and hydroplaning
wrong: Better grip on wet roads
Shorter stopping distance on dry roads
Better fuel economy on long trips
questions.explanation: Worn tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder on wet roads, and can cause hydroplaning.
questions.manual_quote: Worn tires can also cause hydroplaning, and increase the chance of a flat tire.

questions.question: You use a penny to check your tire tread. When does the tire need to be replaced?
questions.answer: When the tread does not reach Lincoln's head (2/32 inch)
wrong: When the tread covers all of Lincoln's head and reaches his hairline
When the tread reaches the top of the penny (1 inch)
When the penny will not fit into the tread at all
questions.explanation: Stick the penny in head first. If the tread does not reach at least to Lincoln's head (2/32 inch), the tire is illegal and unsafe.
questions.manual_quote: If the tread does not come at least to Lincoln’s head (2/32 inch), the tire is illegal and unsafe and you need it replaced.

questions.question: On many newer cars, where can you find the recommended tire pressure?
questions.answer: On a sticker in the driver's side front door jamb
wrong: Printed on the side of the tire itself
On the gas cap
On the sticker on your license plate
questions.explanation: The sticker is usually in the driver's side front door jamb. Do not use the pressure printed on the tire, which is the maximum.
questions.manual_quote: On many newer cars the vehicle’s recommended tire pressure is on the sticker in the door jamb.

questions.question: Should you fill your tires to the pressure printed on the tires themselves?
questions.answer: No, that number is the tire's maximum pressure
wrong: Yes, that number is always the correct pressure
Yes, but only in cold weather
Yes, add 5 psi more than that number
questions.explanation: The psi on the tire is the maximum recommended pressure and may not match your vehicle maker's specifications.
questions.manual_quote: Do not use the tire pressure psi printed on the tires themselves. This is the maximum recommended pressure for the tire

questions.question: Why should you never turn the ignition to the "lock" position while the vehicle is moving?
questions.answer: The steering wheel will lock and you will lose control
wrong: The radio and lights will turn off
The doors will lock automatically and trap everyone inside the car
The brakes will stop working right away
questions.explanation: Turning to "lock" while moving locks the steering wheel in place, and you will lose control.
questions.manual_quote: Never turn your vehicle’s ignition to the “lock” position while the vehicle is in motion.

questions.question: Your car keeps bouncing after you go over a bump. What might it need?
questions.answer: New shocks or other suspension parts
wrong: New windshield wipers
A new battery
More air in the tires and new spark plugs
questions.explanation: If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or stop, or is hard to control, you may need new shocks or suspension parts.
questions.manual_quote: If the vehicle continues to bounce after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, you may need new shocks

questions.question: You and your passengers often feel sleepy while riding in your car. What might be the problem?
questions.answer: An exhaust leak
wrong: Low tire pressure
Worn windshield wipers
A weak horn
questions.explanation: A sleepy feeling may mean an exhaust leak. Gases from a leaky exhaust can cause death quickly. Repair it right away.
questions.manual_quote: you and/or your passengers tend to get a sleepy feeling when driving or riding in your car you may have an exhaust leak

questions.question: Your car is stuck in mud or snow. Why is it dangerous to sit in it with the motor running?
questions.answer: The exhaust pipe may be blocked, trapping deadly fumes
wrong: The engine will run out of oil
The tires will overheat and pop from the heat
The battery will go dead in just a few minutes and the car will not restart
questions.explanation: Never run the motor where the exhaust pipe may be blocked, including a car stuck in mud or snow. Carbon monoxide can overcome people fast.
questions.manual_quote: where the exhaust (tail) pipe may be obstructed. This includes a car that is stuck in mud or snow.

questions.question: When should you check your radiator?
questions.answer: Only when the vehicle is cool
wrong: Right after you turn off the engine
While the engine is running at high speed
Only on very hot days
questions.explanation: Check your radiator ONLY when the vehicle is cool, not right after driving.
questions.manual_quote: Be careful to check your radiator ONLY when the vehicle is cool, not immediately after operation.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?
questions.answer: Only as a warning to others
wrong: To tell slow drivers to hurry up
To greet friends you see on the road
To show other drivers you are upset
questions.explanation: The horn is a warning device. Only use it to warn others.
questions.manual_quote: ONLY use your horn as a warning to others.

questions.question: How much gas should you have before starting a long trip?
questions.answer: At least a half tank
wrong: At least a quarter tank
At least an eighth of a tank
Just enough to reach the next exit
questions.explanation: Have at least a half tank before any trip of significant length. Running out of gas on the road is dangerous.
questions.manual_quote: Be sure your vehicle always has at least a half tank of gas before starting any trip of significant length.

questions.question: When do collisions involving several vehicles often happen?
questions.answer: When drivers go faster or slower than other traffic
wrong: When all drivers move at the same speed
When drivers keep a two-second following distance from the car ahead
When drivers stay in the right lane
questions.explanation: Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another. Crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than traffic.
questions.manual_quote: Collisions involving multiple vehicles often happen when drivers go faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.question: Under Tennessee law, who counts as a pedestrian?
questions.answer: Any person on foot or using a wheelchair
wrong: Only people walking inside a crosswalk
Only people walking on a sidewalk
Only children and elderly people on foot
questions.explanation: Any person on foot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair is a pedestrian under state law.
questions.manual_quote: Any person afoot or using a motorized or nonmotorized wheelchair are considered a pedestrian by state law.

questions.question: Is there a crosswalk at an intersection that has no painted lines?
questions.answer: Yes, every intersection has a crosswalk, marked or not
wrong: No, a crosswalk exists only where white lines are painted on the road
Only if there is a WALK signal at the corner
Only if there is a school or park nearby
questions.explanation: There is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if painted lines do not mark it. Generally, pedestrians have the right of way at intersections.
questions.manual_quote: There is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if painted lines and boundaries do not mark the crossing.

questions.question: You are stopped at a red light. Where should your car be?
questions.answer: Behind the crosswalk, not over any part of it
wrong: With your front bumper over the crosswalk
In the middle of the crosswalk
Past the crosswalk so you can see better
questions.explanation: Don't block the crosswalk or stop with any part of your car over it. It forces pedestrians to walk around your car.
questions.manual_quote: You also should not stop with a portion of your vehicle over the crosswalk area.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk?
questions.answer: When the person is on your half of the road or close enough to be in danger
wrong: Only when the pedestrian has a WALK signal
Only when the pedestrian waves at you
Only when the pedestrian is already standing directly in front of your car's bumper
questions.explanation: Slow down or stop for a pedestrian who is on your half of the road, or who is so close on the other half that they could be in danger.
questions.manual_quote: yield to a pedestrian crossing the roadway within a crosswalk when the pedestrian is upon half of the roadway which you are traveling

questions.question: In a marked school zone with the warning flashers on, a pedestrian is crossing in the crosswalk. What must you do?
questions.answer: Stop and stay stopped until the person has crossed
wrong: Slow down and drive carefully around the pedestrian
Honk and wait for the pedestrian to hurry
Stop only if the pedestrian is a child
questions.explanation: In a school zone with flashers on, you must stop for a pedestrian in the crosswalk and remain stopped until they have crossed. It's the law.
questions.manual_quote: You shall remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway on which your vehicle is stopped.

questions.question: A pedestrian is using a white cane with a red tip or a guide dog. What must you do?
questions.answer: Always yield to the pedestrian
wrong: Honk so the pedestrian knows where you are
Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk
Drive around the pedestrian slowly
questions.explanation: Always yield to blind pedestrians carrying a white or red-tipped white cane or using a guide dog.
questions.manual_quote: Always yield to blind pedestrians carrying a white, metallic, red tipped white cane or using a guide dog.

questions.question: You are pulling out of a driveway or alley across a sidewalk. Someone is walking on the sidewalk. What should you do?
questions.answer: Yield to the pedestrian on the sidewalk
wrong: Honk so the pedestrian moves out of the way
Keep going, since pedestrians must yield to cars
Speed up to cross the sidewalk before they get there
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk when entering or leaving a driveway, parking garage, alley, or parking lot.
questions.manual_quote: Yield to pedestrians walking on the sidewalk when you’re entering or leaving a driveway, public parking garage, alley or parking lot

questions.question: A pedestrian is walking slowly in front of your car, and you have the right of way. What should you do?
questions.answer: Wait patiently without honking or revving your engine
wrong: Honk to tell the pedestrian to hurry
Rev your engine so the pedestrian knows you are waiting
Inch forward slowly to make the pedestrian move
questions.explanation: Don't honk, rev your engine, or do anything to rush or scare a pedestrian, even if you have the right of way.
questions.manual_quote: Don’t honk your horn, rev up your engine or do anything to rush or scare a pedestrian in front of your car

questions.question: When should you be especially watchful for pedestrians to the right of your car?
questions.answer: When you are making a right turn
wrong: When you are backing out of a garage
When you are driving on the interstate
When you are stopped at a railroad crossing
questions.explanation: Be alert to pedestrians on your right, and be especially watchful when making a right turn.
questions.manual_quote: Be alert to pedestrians to the right of your vehicle and be especially watchful for pedestrians when you are making a right turn.

questions.question: Which pedestrians are often the least predictable and the hardest to see?
questions.answer: Children
wrong: Joggers
Adults with umbrellas
Crossing guards
questions.explanation: Children are often the least predictable and most difficult to see. Take extra care near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks.
questions.manual_quote: Children are often the least predictable pedestrians and the most difficult to see.

questions.question: When there is no sidewalk, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on?
questions.answer: The left side, facing oncoming traffic
wrong: The right side, with traffic behind them
Either side, as long as they wear bright clothes
In the middle of the lane so drivers see them
questions.explanation: With no sidewalk, walk on the left side facing traffic so you can see dangers coming. Walk in single file.
questions.manual_quote: When there are no sidewalks, always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic

questions.question: When two or more people walk along a road with no sidewalk, how should they walk?
questions.answer: In single file
wrong: Side by side
Three across, holding hands
In the middle of the lane
questions.explanation: Two or more pedestrians should walk in single file, never side by side.
questions.manual_quote: Two or more pedestrians should walk in single file and never side by side of each other.

questions.question: Before a pedestrian crosses a street, in what order should they look?
questions.answer: Left, right, then left again
wrong: Right, left, then right again
Straight ahead only
Left only
questions.explanation: Stop at the curb or edge, look left-right-left, and if it's clear, begin crossing. Watch for turning vehicles.
questions.manual_quote: Look left-right-left, and if it’s clear, begin crossing, look over your shoulder for turning vehicles.

questions.question: You are walking in the middle of the street and the DON'T WALK signal starts flashing. What should you do?
questions.answer: Keep walking, because there is time to finish
wrong: Turn around and go back to the curb you started from
Stop where you are and wait for the next WALK signal
Run diagonally to the nearest corner
questions.explanation: If the DON'T WALK signal starts flashing while you are in the street, continue walking. You will have time to finish.
questions.manual_quote: If you are in the middle of the street and the DON”T WALK signal starts flashing, continue walking.

questions.question: What does a WALK signal or green light mean for a pedestrian?
questions.answer: It is your turn, but look and cross only if it is safe
wrong: It is always safe to cross without looking
Cars must stop, so you do not need to look first
You must run across quickly before the light changes back to red
questions.explanation: WALK and green mean it's your turn, but do NOT mean it is safe. Look, and if it's safe, cross.
questions.manual_quote: indicate that it’s your turn to cross the street, but they do NOT mean it is SAFE to cross.

questions.question: Should a pedestrian walk behind a truck that is backing up?
questions.answer: No, truck drivers cannot see directly behind the truck
wrong: Yes, if the pedestrian walks quickly
Yes, the backup alarm means the driver sees you
Yes, if the pedestrian waves at the driver first and gets a wave back
questions.explanation: Never walk behind a truck when it is backing up. Truck drivers cannot see directly behind the truck.
questions.manual_quote: Never walk behind a truck when it is backing up; truck drivers cannot see directly behind the truck

questions.question: What is the safest way for a pedestrian to be seen at night?
questions.answer: Carry a flashlight
wrong: Wear dark clothes
Walk on the right side with traffic
Walk close to parked cars
questions.explanation: Wear bright or reflective clothing at night. Carrying a flashlight is your safest bet for being seen.
questions.manual_quote: Carrying a flashlight is your safest bet for being seen at night.

questions.question: On which side of the road must bicyclists ride?
questions.answer: The right side, in the same direction as traffic
wrong: The left side, facing the oncoming traffic
Either side, whichever is safer
Only on the sidewalk
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must ride on the right side in the same direction as vehicles, as close to the right as practical.
questions.manual_quote: Bicyclists are required to travel on the right hand side of the road and travel in the same direction as vehicles.

questions.question: Where are bicyclists NOT allowed to ride?
questions.answer: On limited-access highways and expressways
wrong: On city streets that have parked cars
On two-lane country roads with no shoulder
On residential streets
questions.explanation: Bicyclists are prohibited on limited-access highways, expressways, and certain other marked roadways.
questions.manual_quote: Bicyclists are prohibited on limited-access highways, expressways and certain other marked roadways.

questions.question: A bicyclist moves away from parked cars toward the center of the lane. What does this mean?
questions.answer: The rider is riding properly to avoid opening car doors
wrong: The rider is being careless and breaking the law
The rider wants you to pass on the right
The rider is about to stop
questions.explanation: Cyclists move away from parked cars to avoid people getting out of them. In such cases the bicyclist is riding properly.
questions.manual_quote: In such cases, the bicyclist is operating the bicycle properly.

questions.question: When you pass a bicyclist going the same direction, how much space does Tennessee law require?
questions.answer: At least 3 feet
wrong: At least 1 foot
At least 2 feet
At least 10 feet
questions.explanation: Pass slowly and leave at least 3 feet between you and the bicycle. Keep that space until you are safely past.
questions.manual_quote: leave at least a distance between you and the bicycle of not less than 3 feet. It’s the law in Tennessee!

questions.question: On a two-lane road, you are behind a bicyclist and a car is coming toward you. What should you do?
questions.answer: Slow down and wait, and never pass between the bike and oncoming cars
wrong: Pass quickly between the bicyclist and the oncoming car
Honk so the bicyclist pulls off the road and stops
Flash your lights so the oncoming car moves over to the right shoulder
questions.explanation: Never try to pass between a bicyclist and oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road. Slow down and wait.
questions.manual_quote: A driver should never attempt passing between a bicyclist and oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road.

questions.question: You are about to pass a bicyclist on a narrow road, and the rider may not know you are there. What should you do?
questions.answer: Tap your horn gently and briefly
wrong: Blast your horn so the rider moves over
Flash your high beams at the rider
Pass without any warning at all
questions.explanation: Tap your horn gently and briefly as a signal. Don't blast your horn or try to startle the bicyclist.
questions.manual_quote: tap your horn gently and briefly as a signal that you’re going to pass.

questions.question: You are turning left, and a bicyclist is entering the intersection from the opposite direction. What should you do?
questions.answer: Wait for the bicyclist to pass before you turn
wrong: Turn quickly in front of the bicyclist
Honk and then make your turn
Turn, since cars have the right of way over bicycles
questions.explanation: Turning left in front of an oncoming bicycle is one of the most common causes of collisions. Wait for the rider to pass.
questions.manual_quote: you should wait for the bicyclist to pass before making the turn.

questions.question: You are turning right, and a bicyclist is coming up on your right. What should you do?
questions.answer: Let the bicyclist go through the intersection first
wrong: Turn right in front of the bicyclist
Speed up so you can turn before the bicyclist arrives
Stop in the bike lane and wave the rider around
questions.explanation: Let the bicyclist go through first, then turn. Don't turn directly across the bicyclist's path.
questions.manual_quote: If your vehicle is turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on the right, let the bicyclist go through the intersection first

questions.question: At night, a bicyclist is coming toward you. What should you do with your headlights?
questions.answer: Do not use high beams
wrong: Switch to high beams so you can see the rider
Flash your high beams to warn the rider
Turn your headlights off until the rider passes
questions.explanation: At night, do not use high beams when you see an oncoming bicycle rider.
questions.manual_quote: At night, do not use high beams when you see an oncoming bicycle rider.

questions.question: A bicyclist holds the left arm straight out to the side. What does this signal mean?
questions.answer: The rider is turning left
wrong: The rider is turning right
The rider is stopping or slowing
The rider wants you to pass
questions.explanation: For a left turn, the rider extends the left arm straight out sideways or points left.
questions.manual_quote: Extend your left arm out sideways with all fingers extended or use your index finger to point left.

questions.question: A bicyclist holds the left arm out, bent up at the elbow, hand pointing upward. What does this signal mean?
questions.answer: Right turn
wrong: Left turn
Stopping or slowing
Go ahead and pass
questions.explanation: Left arm bent upward at 90 degrees means right turn. A rider may also point the right arm straight out to the right.
questions.manual_quote: Right Turn Extend your left arm out sideways bent at a 90-degree angle at the elbow joint, hand pointing upward

questions.question: A bicyclist holds an arm out, bent down at the elbow, hand pointing downward. What does this signal mean?
questions.answer: The rider is stopping or slowing
wrong: The rider is turning left
The rider is turning right
The rider is waving you on to pass
questions.explanation: An arm bent downward at 90 degrees with the palm facing back means the rider is stopping or slowing.
questions.manual_quote: bend your arm at a 90-degree angle at the elbow joint, hand pointing downwards

questions.question: Tennessee law says a bicycle ridden at night must have a white front lamp visible from how far?
questions.answer: At least 500 feet
wrong: At least 50 feet
At least 100 feet
At least 1,000 feet
questions.explanation: A bicycle used at night needs a white front lamp visible at least 500 feet ahead, plus a red rear reflector or lamp visible 500 feet behind.
questions.manual_quote: a lamp on the front that emits a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet

questions.question: What must a bicycle used at night have on the rear?
questions.answer: A red reflector or red lamp visible from 500 feet
wrong: A white lamp visible from 100 feet
A yellow flag on a tall pole
A flashing blue light visible from 200 feet
questions.explanation: At night a bicycle needs a red reflector or a lamp with red light visible from 500 feet to the rear.
questions.manual_quote: either a red reflector or lamp emitting a red light that is visible from distance of 500 feet to the rear

questions.question: You see a bicyclist with a red or orange pennant flag on the bike. What does it usually mean, and what should you do?
questions.answer: The rider has impaired hearing, so slow down
wrong: The rider is in a race, so speed up and pass
The rider is a police officer, so pull over
The rider is towing a trailer, so honk
questions.explanation: A red or orange pennant flag is a common symbol that the rider has impaired hearing. Slow down.
questions.manual_quote: If you see a bicyclist with a red or orange pennant flag on the antennae attached to the bike, slow down

questions.question: A lane is marked and signed for bicycle use only. May you use it as a turning lane, passing lane, or for parking?
questions.answer: No, never use a bike lane for turning, passing, or parking
wrong: Yes, you may park in it for up to 15 minutes
Yes, you may use it to pass slow cars on the right if you signal
Yes, if no bicyclists are in sight
questions.explanation: Drivers must NEVER use a marked bicycle-only lane as a turning lane, passing lane, or for parking.
questions.manual_quote: drivers must NEVER use this lane as a turning lane, passing lane or for parking.

questions.question: The lane is too narrow for a car and a bicycle to share safely. What is safest?
questions.answer: Let the bicycle take the full lane
wrong: Squeeze past the bicycle in the same lane
Honk so the bicycle rides on the shoulder
Drive beside the bicycle until the lane widens
questions.explanation: When the lane is too narrow for both to share safely, it is safest to let the bicycle take the full lane.
questions.manual_quote: In this case it is safest to let the bicycle take the full lane.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra careful around children riding bicycles?
questions.answer: Children may move suddenly or change direction without warning
wrong: Children always signal before they turn
Children are required to ride on the sidewalk
Children ride slower than adults, so they are never a risk to drivers
questions.explanation: Children are not capable of proper judgment about traffic, so be alert for erratic movement and sudden direction changes.
questions.manual_quote: drivers should be alert to the possibility of erratic movement and sudden changes in direction when children on bicycles are present.

questions.question: In crashes between cars and motorcycles, what causes about two-thirds of them?
questions.answer: A car driver turning in front of the motorcycle
wrong: The motorcyclist speeding
The motorcyclist riding without a helmet on
Bad weather and slippery roads at night
questions.explanation: Two-thirds of car-motorcycle collisions are caused by the driver who turned in front of the motorcycle, often because they didn't see it.
questions.manual_quote: two-thirds of car-motorcycle collisions are caused, not by the motorcyclist, but by the driver who turned in front of the motorcycle.

questions.question: May you share a lane with a motorcycle?
questions.answer: No, a motorcycle has the right to the full lane
wrong: Yes, if the motorcycle is riding near the edge
Yes, on roads with a speed limit over 45 mph
Yes, if you are both going the same speed
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane. You must never try to share a lane with a motorcycle.
questions.manual_quote: Motorcycles have the right to the use of the full lane.

questions.question: What following distance should you allow behind a motorcycle?
questions.answer: At least two seconds
wrong: At least half a second
At least one second
One car length
questions.explanation: Allow at least a two-second following distance so the rider has time to maneuver or stop in an emergency.
questions.manual_quote: Allow at least a two-second following distance, so the motorcycle rider has enough time to maneuver or stop in an emergency.

questions.question: When should you allow more following distance for motorcycles?
questions.answer: When the road surface is wet and slippery
wrong: When the road is dry and clear
When the motorcycle has its headlight on
When you are driving in the daytime
questions.explanation: Bad weather and slippery surfaces cause greater problems for motorcycles. Allow more following distance on wet roads.
questions.manual_quote: Allow more following distance for cyclists when the road surface is wet and slippery.

questions.question: At an intersection with a motorcycle, when should you move into its path of travel?
questions.answer: Only after the rider's intentions are absolutely clear
wrong: As soon as the motorcycle slows down
Whenever the motorcycle's turn signal is blinking, even if it is not turning yet
As soon as you see a gap in car traffic
questions.explanation: Most collisions happen at intersections. Wait until it is absolutely clear whether the rider is turning or going straight.
questions.manual_quote: wait until the rider’s intentions are absolutely clear (turning or going straight) before you move into the path of travel.

questions.question: Why is it easy to misjudge a motorcycle's distance at night?
questions.answer: Its single headlight or tail light can blend in with other lights
wrong: Motorcycles are not required to have lights at night
Motorcycle lights are always brighter than car lights
Motorcycles use green lights at night, which are hard to see in traffic
questions.explanation: The single headlight or tail light of a motorcycle can blend into other lights. Always dim your headlights as you would for other vehicles.
questions.manual_quote: the single headlight or single tail light of a motorcycle can blend into the lights of other vehicles.

questions.question: How do metal or grated bridges affect motorcycles?
questions.answer: They make a motorcycle wobble much more than a car
wrong: They give motorcycles better grip than cars
They have no effect on motorcycles
They make motorcycles go faster
questions.explanation: Metal or grated bridges make a motorcycle wobble. Experienced riders slow down and move to the center of the lane.
questions.manual_quote: Metal or grated bridges cause a cycle to wobble much more than a car.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist tell if a helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards?
questions.answer: Check for the DOT label inside the helmet
wrong: Check that the helmet is painted bright orange
Check that the helmet has a face shield
Check that the helmet weighs over 5 pounds
questions.explanation: Beware of helmets that do not meet DOT standards. Check for the DOT label inside your helmet.
questions.manual_quote: Check for the DOT label inside your helmet.

questions.question: You cannot see the truck driver in the truck's side mirror. What does that tell you?
questions.answer: The truck driver cannot see you
wrong: The truck driver can see you clearly
The truck's mirror is broken
You are at a safe distance from the truck
questions.explanation: If you can't see the truck driver in the truck's mirror, the truck driver can't see you. You are in a No-Zone.
questions.manual_quote: if you can’t see the truck driver in the truck’s mirror, the truck driver can’t see you.

questions.question: What is a "squeeze play" with a truck?
questions.answer: Getting caught between a right-turning truck and the curb
wrong: Passing a truck on a downhill grade
Following a truck too closely while going up a steep hill
Driving between two trucks in different lanes
questions.explanation: Trucks swing wide to the left to make a right turn. If you get between the truck and the curb, you can be caught in a squeeze.
questions.manual_quote: If you try to get in between the truck and the curb, you’ll be caught in a “squeeze” and can suffer a serious accident.

questions.question: What is the single most important thing you can do to save your life in a crash, especially with a large truck?
questions.answer: Wear a safety belt
wrong: Turn on your hazard lights
Let go of the steering wheel
Lean toward the passenger seat
questions.explanation: Your safety belt keeps you from hitting the steering wheel or windshield and from being thrown from the car.
questions.manual_quote: Wearing a safety belt is the single most important thing you can do to save your life

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots, or No-Zones?
questions.answer: Right in front, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind
wrong: Only directly behind the truck, up to 20 feet
Only on the left side of the cab, near the driver's door
Only in front of the truck, up to 500 feet
questions.explanation: A truck's blind spots are immediately in front, on either side, and up to 200 feet in the rear.
questions.manual_quote: A truck’s blind spots are immediate in front, on either side of the car and up to 200 feet in the rear.

questions.question: If a tractor has a long hood, how much of the road directly in front of the bumper may the trucker be unable to see?
questions.answer: The first 10 to 20 feet
wrong: The first 1 to 2 feet
The first 50 to 60 feet
The first 200 feet
questions.explanation: With a long hood, the trucker may not see the first 10-20 feet in front of the bumper, enough room for a car to slip in unnoticed.
questions.manual_quote: the trucker may not be able to see the first 10-20 feet in front of the bumper

questions.question: You are stopped behind a truck on an uphill grade. What should you do?
questions.answer: Stay left in your lane and leave extra space in case it rolls back
wrong: Pull up as close as you can to the truck's back bumper
Stay to the far right in your lane so the truck driver can see you better
Honk so the truck driver knows you are there
questions.explanation: Stay left in your lane so the driver can see you, and leave extra space in front in case the truck rolls back.
questions.manual_quote: If you are stopped behind a truck on an uphill grade, stay to the left in your lane so the driver can see you.

questions.question: A car at 55 mph can stop in about 240 feet. About how far does a truck at 55 mph need to stop?
questions.answer: About 450 feet or more
wrong: About 240 feet, the same as a car
About 150 feet
About 1 mile
questions.explanation: Trucks take much longer to stop. At 55 mph, a car stops in about 240 feet, but a truck needs about 450 feet or more.
questions.manual_quote: can stop in 240 feet however a truck traveling at the same speed of 55 MPH, takes about 450+ feet to stop.

questions.question: How do large trucks make a right turn?
questions.answer: They swing wide to the left first, then turn right
wrong: They pull onto the right shoulder, then turn
They make a tight turn close to the curb
They stop and back into the turn
questions.explanation: Trucks must swing wide to the left to make a right turn. Know which way the truck is turning before you try to pass.
questions.manual_quote: Trucks must swing wide to the left to safely negotiate a right turn.

questions.question: You are passing a large truck. When is it safe to pull back in front of it?
questions.answer: When you can see the whole front of the truck in your mirror
wrong: As soon as your back bumper clears the truck's front bumper by a foot
When you are halfway past the truck
When the truck driver honks the horn
questions.explanation: Do NOT pull back in front of the truck until you can see the whole front of it in your rearview mirror. Do not slow down after you pull in.
questions.manual_quote: unless you can see the whole front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: After you pass a truck, the truck driver blinks the headlights. What does that usually mean?
questions.answer: You are cleared to pull back in front of the truck
wrong: You must pull over and stop
The truck is about to pass you back on the left side
Your own headlights are off
questions.explanation: Blinking headlights after you pass signal that you are cleared to move back in. Still wait until you see the truck's front in your mirror.
questions.manual_quote: blink their vehicle headlights after you pass, it’s a signal that you are cleared to pull back in front

questions.question: You have just passed a truck and moved back in front of it. What should you do with your speed?
questions.answer: Keep your speed, and do not slow down in front of the truck
wrong: Slow down so the truck can pass you back
Tap your brakes a few times to thank the truck driver
Stop quickly to let the truck exit
questions.explanation: Do NOT slow down once you are in front of the truck. It forces the truck driver to brake, which is dangerous.
questions.manual_quote: Do NOT slow down once you are in front of the truck.

questions.question: How does a large truck's speed usually change on hills?
questions.answer: It loses speed going uphill and travels faster going downhill
wrong: It speeds up going uphill and slows down going downhill
It keeps exactly the same speed on all hills
It slows down by the same amount on both uphill and downhill grades
questions.explanation: On an upgrade a large vehicle usually loses speed. Because of their weight, trucks travel faster downhill.
questions.manual_quote: Remember that on an upgrade or steep hill, a large vehicle usually loses speed.

questions.question: You are driving near a Commercial Vehicle Weigh Station. Which lane should you avoid?
questions.answer: The right lane
wrong: The left lane
The center lane
The shoulder lane
questions.explanation: Avoid the right lane near a weigh station so slow-moving trucks can easily merge back onto the road.
questions.manual_quote: When you are near a Commercial Vehicle Weigh Station, avoid driving in the right lane

questions.question: You are following a truck at night. What should you do with your headlights?
questions.answer: Dim them, since bright lights in its mirrors can blind the driver
wrong: Use high beams so the truck driver can see you clearly in the mirrors
Flash them so the truck driver knows you are there
Turn them off and use parking lights
questions.explanation: Dim your lights at night. Bright lights reflected in the truck's mirrors can blind the driver.
questions.manual_quote: Dim your lights at night. Bright lights reflected in the mirrors can blind the driver.

questions.question: Why can it be hard to judge how fast a truck or bus is moving?
questions.answer: Their large size makes them seem slower than they really are
wrong: Their large size makes them seem faster than they really are
Trucks are not allowed to use turn signals
Trucks always drive at exactly the speed limit
questions.explanation: Never underestimate the size and speed of trucks and buses. Their large size often makes them appear slower than their real speed.
questions.manual_quote: Because of their large size they often appear to be traveling more slowly than their actual speed.

questions.question: You want to exit the highway, but a large truck is beside you. What should you do?
questions.answer: Slow down and exit behind the truck
wrong: Speed up and cut in front of the truck to exit
Cut sharply in front of the truck while signaling
Stop in your lane until the truck moves
questions.explanation: Do NOT cut abruptly in front of a large vehicle. It only takes a few extra seconds to slow down and exit behind the truck.
questions.manual_quote: If you are exiting, it will only take a few extra seconds to slow down and exit behind the truck.

questions.question: A truck is coming toward you from the opposite direction. What should you do?
questions.answer: Keep as far right as you can to avoid wind and being sideswiped
wrong: Move toward the centerline so the wind does not push you off the road
Speed up to get past the truck quickly
Stop in your lane until the truck passes
questions.explanation: Keep far to the right. The wind between vehicles PUSHES them APART. It does not pull them together.
questions.manual_quote: keep as far as possible to the right of the road to avoid being sideswiped and to reduce wind turbulence between vehicles.

questions.question: A truck is passing you. What can you do to help?
questions.answer: Keep to the far side of your lane and slow down a bit
wrong: Speed up so you stay even with the truck as it passes
Move toward the truck so it has less room
Brake hard so the truck gets by faster
questions.explanation: Keep to the far side of your lane and reduce speed slightly. NEVER speed up as a truck or bus is passing.
questions.manual_quote: When a truck passes you, you can help the driver by keeping to the far side of your lane and reducing your speed slightly.

questions.question: A truck ahead of you has its right turn signal on and has left an open space on its right side. What should you do?
questions.answer: Stay out of that space and do not pass on the right
wrong: Move into that space to get ahead of the truck
Pass the truck quickly on the right
Honk so the truck lets you through
questions.explanation: Trucks making wide right turns leave space on the right. Do NOT move into it, because the trailer could crunch or sideswipe your car.
questions.manual_quote: Do NOT move into that space or try to pass a truck if it might be making a right turn.

questions.question: A truck is preparing to back into a loading dock and is blocking the road. What should you do?
questions.answer: Wait patiently, and never cross behind the backing truck
wrong: Drive quickly behind the truck before it moves
Honk so the truck driver lets you pass
Drive around the truck on the sidewalk
questions.explanation: Never cross behind a truck preparing to back up. You will be in the driver's blind spots. Wait the few minutes it takes.
questions.manual_quote: Never try to cross behind a truck when it is preparing to back up.

questions.question: About how far in front of a large vehicle is considered a NO-ZONE?
questions.answer: Up to about 20 feet
wrong: Up to about 2 feet
Up to about 100 feet
Up to about 500 feet
questions.explanation: The area up to about 20 feet directly in front of a large vehicle is a NO-ZONE. Don't cut in too soon after passing.
questions.manual_quote: The area approximately up to 20 feet directly in front of a large vehicle is considered a NO-ZONE.

questions.question: Spray from a truck on a wet road is blocking your view. What should you do?
questions.answer: Move as far from the truck as you can while staying in your lane
wrong: Move closer to the truck to stay out of the spray
Change into the truck's lane and follow right behind it
Turn on your high beams so you can see through the spray more clearly
questions.explanation: Spray from a truck seriously reduces your vision. Move as far away from the truck as you can while staying in your lane.
questions.manual_quote: You should move as far away from the truck as you can, while staying in your lane.

questions.question: Why should you not drive too close to trucks carrying hazardous materials?
questions.answer: They make frequent stops, such as at railroad crossings
wrong: They are not allowed to use brake lights
They always drive faster than the speed limit
They may only drive in the left lane
questions.explanation: Trucks carrying hazardous materials make frequent stops, such as at railroad crossings.
questions.manual_quote: Don’t drive too close to trucks that are transporting hazardous materials, since they make frequent stops, such as railroad crossings.

questions.question: On a steep hill, you see a truck with smoking wheels or going very fast. What should you do?
questions.answer: Fall back and do NOT pass
wrong: Pass the truck as quickly as you can
Pull in close behind the truck
Honk to warn the truck driver
questions.explanation: Smoking wheels or high speed can be a sign of brake loss. Fall back and do NOT pass.
questions.manual_quote: Smoking wheels or a high speed can be a sign of brake loss. If you encounter this situation, fall back and DO NOT pass.

questions.question: May you stop or park on a runaway truck ramp?
questions.answer: No, never stop or park on a runaway truck ramp
wrong: Yes, it is a good place to rest
Yes, in an emergency for up to one hour
Yes, if you turn on your hazard lights
questions.explanation: Runaway truck ramps stop out-of-control trucks on steep downgrades. Vehicles should never stop or park there.
questions.manual_quote: Vehicles should never stop or park in these areas.

questions.question: How far away from a school bus should children stay?
questions.answer: Ten feet
wrong: Two feet
Five feet
Fifty feet
questions.explanation: The Danger Zone is on all sides of the bus. Children should stay ten feet away and NEVER go behind the bus.
questions.manual_quote: Children should stay ten feet away from the school bus and NEVER go behind the bus.

questions.question: Children are taught to take "five giant steps" away from the school bus. What does this mean for drivers?
questions.answer: Stop far enough from the bus to leave room for that space
wrong: Stop right next to the bus so the children can see you and your car
Drive past slowly once children take five steps
Honk so children take their steps faster
questions.explanation: Drivers must know the Danger Zone and stop far enough from the bus to allow for the five-giant-step safety space.
questions.manual_quote: drivers must ensure that they stop far enough from the bus to allow for this needed safety space.

questions.question: What does the "slow moving vehicle" emblem look like?
questions.answer: A fluorescent or reflective orange triangle
wrong: A red octagon
A yellow diamond with a black border
A white rectangle
questions.explanation: The slow moving vehicle emblem is an orange triangle on the rear of animal-drawn vehicles and most farm and construction vehicles.
questions.manual_quote: The “slow moving vehicle” emblem, a fluorescent or reflective orange triangle, must be displayed on the rear of vehicles drawn by animals

questions.question: How fast is farm machinery usually traveling on the road?
questions.answer: Less than 25 mph
wrong: About 35 mph
About 45 mph
The posted speed limit
questions.explanation: In most cases farm machinery travels at less than 25 mph. Be ready to find it over the top of a hill.
questions.manual_quote: In most cases, these vehicles will be traveling at less than 25 M.P.H.

questions.question: How might a farm tractor make a right turn?
questions.answer: It may first pull wide to the left, then turn right
wrong: It always uses a right turn signal and turns tightly
It pulls onto the right shoulder and stops first
It backs up and then turns right
questions.explanation: Farm machinery usually does not have turn signals. To turn right, the operator may first pull wide to the left.
questions.manual_quote: to make a right turn, operators of farm machinery may first pull wide to the left, then turn to the right.

questions.question: Do horse-drawn vehicles have the right to use the road?
questions.answer: Yes, they have the same rights as a motor vehicle
wrong: No, they must stay on the shoulder at all times
Only on roads with no speed limit
Only during daylight hours
questions.explanation: Animal-drawn vehicles have the same rights to use the road as motor vehicles and must follow the same rules.
questions.manual_quote: They have the same rights to use the road as a motor vehicle and must follow the same rules of the road.

questions.question: You are approaching a person riding a horse along the road. What should you NOT do?
questions.answer: Sound your horn or rev your engine loudly
wrong: Slow to a reasonable speed
Leave a reasonable distance from the horse
Use due care as you pass
questions.explanation: Drive at a reasonable speed and distance from the horse. Do NOT sound your horn or rev your engine loudly.
questions.manual_quote: Do NOT sound your horn or “rev” your engine loudly when approaching or passing a horse.

questions.question: What is the normal speed range for slow-moving vehicles?
questions.answer: 5 to 20 mph
wrong: 25 to 35 mph
30 to 45 mph
1 to 3 mph
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles normally go 5 to 20 mph, so you close in on them very fast at highway speed.
questions.manual_quote: Normal speeds for slow-moving vehicles may range from 5 to 20 mph.

questions.question: Before you pass a slow-moving vehicle, what should you make sure of?
questions.answer: That the driver has seen you and knows you plan to pass
wrong: That you honk loudly three times
That you are going at least 20 mph faster
That the slow vehicle has pulled all the way onto the shoulder first
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles may turn at any time into unmarked entrances. Stay back until it is safe, and be sure the driver sees you.
questions.manual_quote: be certain the driver has seen you and is aware of your intent to pass before you begin.

questions.question: When lights are required on a slow-moving vehicle, what is normally on the rear?
questions.answer: A red lamp visible for 500 feet
wrong: A white lamp visible for 100 feet
A blue lamp visible for 1,000 feet
A green lamp visible for 200 feet
questions.explanation: A self-luminous red lamp on the rear is normally visible for 500 feet. Some also have red or amber rotating lights.
questions.manual_quote: a self-luminous red lamp on the rear of the vehicle is normally visible for 500 feet to the rear.

questions.question: Which lane must slower traffic use?
questions.answer: The right-hand lane
wrong: The left-hand lane
The center turn lane
Any lane they choose
questions.explanation: Slower traffic must drive in the right-hand lane. The left lane is for passing and turning.
questions.manual_quote: Slower traffic must drive in the right-hand lane. The left lane is for passing and turning.

questions.question: What color is the common theme of highway work zones?
questions.answer: Orange
wrong: Blue
Green
Red
questions.explanation: Orange always means "road work, slow down." Temporary work zone signs have an orange background and black letters or symbols.
questions.manual_quote: The common theme among work zones is the color orange.

questions.question: What do temporary work zone signs look like?
questions.answer: An orange background with black letters or symbols
wrong: A yellow background with red letters
A white background with green letters or symbols
A blue background with white letters
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background and black letters or symbols.
questions.manual_quote: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background and black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What color clothing will highway workers normally wear in work zones?
questions.answer: Bright yellow-green
wrong: Dark blue
Brown
Plain white with black stripes
questions.explanation: Workers normally wear bright yellow-green shirts, vests, or hardhats so they are highly visible.
questions.manual_quote: workers will normally be wearing bright yellow-green apparel such as shirts, vests or hardhats to ensure they are highly visible.

questions.question: You are in a work zone, but no reduced speed limit is posted. What speed should you obey?
questions.answer: The normal posted speed limit
wrong: 10 mph below the normal limit
25 mph
Any speed that keeps up with traffic
questions.explanation: Reduced limits are clearly posted. If there are no reduced speed postings, obey the normal posted speed limit.
questions.manual_quote: if there are no reduced speed limit postings, drivers should obey the normal posted speed limit.

questions.question: In Tennessee, speeding in a work zone where the speed is reduced and workers are present can lead to a fine of up to how much?
questions.explanation: Speed violations in reduced-speed work zones with workers present can result in a fine up to a maximum of $500.
questions.manual_quote: will result in a fine up to a maximum of $500 dollars.

questions.question: A car going 60 mph travels 88 feet per second. You see a sign that says "Road Work 1500 Feet." About how soon will you reach the work zone?
questions.answer: In about 17 seconds
wrong: In about 5 seconds
In about 1 minute
In about 3 minutes
questions.explanation: At 60 mph you travel 88 feet per second, so you will be in the zone 1,500 feet ahead in about 17 seconds.
questions.manual_quote: If you see a sign that says “Road Work 1500 Feet”, you’ll be in that construction zone in 17 seconds!

questions.question: When should you merge for a lane closure ahead in a work zone?
questions.answer: As soon as possible, when you first see the work zone
wrong: At the very last moment before the lane ends
Only after you can see the workers on the road
Only when a flagger tells you to
questions.explanation: Merge as soon as possible. If you wait until the last moment to merge, you can get a ticket and you can cause a crash.
questions.manual_quote: You can be ticketed and the cause of an accident for being a last chance merger.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlights before you enter a work zone?
questions.answer: Turn them on
wrong: Turn them off
Switch to high beams and flash them
Leave them as they are
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights before you enter the zone so workers and other drivers can see you.
questions.manual_quote: Turn your lights on before you enter the zone!

questions.question: May you change lanes inside a work zone?
questions.answer: Only if you are instructed to do so
wrong: Yes, any time traffic slows down
Yes, if you signal first
Yes, if no workers are visible
questions.explanation: Follow the signs and flaggers, and don't change lanes within the work zone unless instructed to do so.
questions.manual_quote: don't change lanes within the work zone unless instructed to do so.

questions.question: What type of crash causes most work zone accidents?
questions.answer: Rear-end collisions
wrong: Head-on collisions
Rollover crashes
Collisions with animals
questions.explanation: Don't tailgate in work zones. Most work zone accidents are caused by rear-end collisions.
questions.manual_quote: Most work zone accidents are caused by rear-end collisions.

questions.question: You passed a work zone warning sign but do not see any workers. How long should you obey the posted work zone signs?
questions.answer: Until you see the sign that says "End Road Work"
wrong: Until you pass the first orange cone
Only while you can see workers
For one mile after the first sign
questions.explanation: Some work zones are mobile. Observe the posted signs until you see the one that says "End Road Work."
questions.manual_quote: Observe the posted signs until you see the one that says “End Road Work”.

questions.question: Who has the right of way at a railroad crossing?
questions.answer: Trains always have the right of way
wrong: The vehicle that arrives first
Cars, if the train is still far away
Whoever is going faster
questions.explanation: Drivers must ALWAYS yield the right of way to trains. It's the law.
questions.manual_quote: Drivers must ALWAYS yield the right of way to trains because IT’S THE LAW.

questions.question: About how far does a train traveling 55 mph need to stop?
questions.answer: A full mile
wrong: About 100 feet
About 500 feet
About one block
questions.explanation: A train at 55 mph takes a full mile to stop. It cannot stop in time or swerve to avoid you.
questions.manual_quote: A train traveling at 55 miles per hour takes a full mile to stop.

questions.question: Which sign tells you a railroad crossing is ahead?
questions.answer: A round yellow sign
wrong: A red octagon sign
An orange triangle sign
A blue rectangle sign
questions.explanation: Railroad warning signs include the round yellow railroad-ahead sign, the crossbuck, pavement markings, and at busy crossings, flashing lights and gates.
questions.manual_quote: These signs include the round yellow railroad ahead crossing sign, the railroad cross-buck sign, pavement markings

questions.question: You come to a railroad crossing with a stop sign. What must you do?
questions.answer: Stop completely and look both ways before crossing
wrong: Slow down, and stop only if you can see a train coming
Stop only if other cars are stopped
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with a stop sign, you must stop completely and cross only after looking both ways for a train.
questions.manual_quote: you must come to a complete stop and proceed across the tracks only after looking both ways

questions.question: The crossing gates are down at a railroad crossing. When may you cross?
questions.answer: Only after the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing
wrong: As soon as the train passes, even if the gates are still down
Whenever you can safely drive around the gates
When the gates start to go up, even if the lights are still flashing
questions.explanation: Never drive around a lowered gate. It is against the law. Wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.
questions.manual_quote: Don’t cross the tracks until the gates are fully raised and the lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with signal devices, where must you stop?
questions.answer: Within 50 feet but no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail
wrong: Within 100 feet but no closer than 50 feet from the nearest rail
Within 10 feet but no closer than 5 feet from the nearest rail
Right at the edge of the nearest rail
questions.explanation: At crossings with electric or mechanical signals, stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
questions.manual_quote: bring the vehicle to a complete stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail

questions.question: You are crossing the tracks, and the warning lights start flashing. What should you do?
questions.answer: Keep moving across the tracks, and never back up
wrong: Stop right where you are
Back up off the tracks as fast as you can
Get out of the car and run
questions.explanation: Don't stop. KEEP MOVING. The signals give enough time to finish crossing, and the far gate will not block you in. Never back up.
questions.manual_quote: If you are crossing the tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or the gates start coming down, don’t stop. KEEP MOVING!

questions.question: Your vehicle stalls on the railroad tracks. What should you do first?
questions.answer: Get everyone out right away and away from the tracks
wrong: Keep trying to restart the car until the engine starts
Stay in the car with your safety belt on
Push the car off the tracks yourself
questions.explanation: All occupants should exit immediately and get away from the tracks, even if you do not see a train.
questions.manual_quote: all occupants should exit the vehicle immediately and get away from the tracks even if you do not see a train.

questions.question: Your car is stalled on the tracks and everyone is out. Who should you call?
questions.answer: The number on the blue ENS sign, or 911 if you can't find it
wrong: A tow truck company, then your insurance company
The nearest gas station, so they can send someone with a jump start
No one, because the train will see your car and stop
questions.explanation: Call the number on the ENS sign and give the DOT crossing number. If you can't find the sign, call 911.
questions.manual_quote: Locate the Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign and call the emergency number provided

questions.question: What color is the Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at a railroad crossing usually?
questions.answer: Blue
wrong: Red
Orange
Green
questions.explanation: The ENS sign is normally blue and may be on the crossbuck post or signal post.
questions.manual_quote: The Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign, normally blue in color and may be located on the crossbuck post or signal post.

questions.question: Your car is stalled on the tracks and a train is coming. Which way should you run?
questions.answer: Toward the train at a 45-degree angle, away from the tracks
wrong: In the same direction the train is going, alongside the tracks
Straight down the middle of the tracks
Back to your car to get your things
questions.explanation: Run toward the train at a 45-degree angle. This keeps you away from and behind the impact point and flying debris.
questions.manual_quote: If a train is approaching, run toward the train at a 45 degree angle.

questions.question: A train has just passed at a crossing with more than one track. What should you do before crossing?
questions.answer: Make sure no other train is coming on another track
wrong: Cross right away, since the train is now gone
Honk your horn, then cross
Follow the car in front of you closely across the tracks
questions.explanation: Where there is more than one track, a second train may be coming. Don't cross until you are sure no other trains are coming.
questions.manual_quote: Don’t go across the tracks until you are sure that no other trains are coming on another track from either direction.

questions.question: Which vehicles must stop at all railroad crossings, whether signals are activated or not?
questions.answer: School buses, passenger buses, and hazardous-materials trucks
wrong: Motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds
Police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances that are on emergency calls
Pickup trucks, vans, and RVs
questions.explanation: These vehicles must stop at all crossings. Never pass them on a two-way road when they are stopped.
questions.manual_quote: School Buses, Passenger Buses and Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop at all crossings whether signals are activated to not.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped at a railroad crossing on a two-way road. May you pass it?
questions.answer: No, never pass it on a two-way road
wrong: Yes, if you honk first
Yes, if the crossing lights are not flashing
Yes, if you can see the tracks are clear
questions.explanation: School buses must stop at all railroad crossings. Never try to pass a stopped school bus there on a two-way road.
questions.manual_quote: Never attempt to pass these stopped vehicles on a two-way road.

questions.question: Who in a 15-passenger van must wear a safety belt in Tennessee?
questions.answer: All occupants, at all times
wrong: Only the driver
Only passengers in the front seats
Only passengers under 18
questions.explanation: All occupants in 15-passenger vans must wear safety belts at all times. This is the law in Tennessee.
questions.manual_quote: All occupants in 15-passenger vans must wear safety belts at all times. This is the law in Tennessee

questions.question: How often should the tires on a 15-passenger van be inspected and the pressure checked?
questions.answer: Every time the van is used
wrong: Once a month
Once a year
Only before long trips
questions.explanation: Check tires every time the van is used. Under-inflated rear tires, especially the left rear, are a major cause of tread separation.
questions.manual_quote: Tires need to be inspected and tire pressure checked every time the van is used.

questions.question: Is a special endorsement or license needed to drive a 15-passenger van in Tennessee?
questions.answer: No, you do not need a special endorsement or license
wrong: Yes, you need a commercial driver license to drive one
Yes, a special van endorsement is required
Yes, but only if you are under 25
questions.explanation: No special endorsement is needed, but drivers should be trained and experienced because these vans handle differently.
questions.manual_quote: There are no special endorsements or licenses needed to operate a 15-passenger van in the State of Tennessee.

questions.question: In a 15-passenger van, where should passengers sit to keep the van more stable?
questions.answer: As far toward the front as possible
wrong: As far toward the back as possible
All on the left side
All on the right side
questions.explanation: Sit as far forward as possible. The rear seat is behind the rear axle, which pushes the center of gravity back.
questions.manual_quote: Have passengers sit as far towards the front of the vehicle as possible.

questions.question: Why should you NOT tow a trailer or put cargo on the roof of a 15-passenger van?
questions.answer: It changes the center of gravity and increases the chance of rollover
wrong: It makes the van use less fuel
It makes the brakes work better
It makes the tires last longer and helps the van stop more quickly
questions.explanation: Towing or roof cargo affects the center of gravity and increases the chance of a rollover.
questions.manual_quote: Do not tow any trailers or put cargo on the roof of the van. These actions also impact the CG, increasing chances of rollover.

questions.question: Your 15-passenger van's tires drop off the edge of the roadway. What should you do?
questions.answer: Gradually slow down and steer back on when it is safe
wrong: Jerk the steering wheel quickly so you get back onto the road right away
Brake as hard as you can right away
Speed up to bounce back onto the road
questions.explanation: Most rollovers happen at high speed with sudden steering. Slow down gradually and steer back on when safe.
questions.manual_quote: If the van’s tires should drop off the roadway, gradually slow down and steer back on to the roadway

questions.question: How should you load heavy items in an RV?
questions.answer: Secure them, keep them low, and spread them evenly on both sides
wrong: Put them up on the roof so you have more space inside the RV
Put them all on one side
Leave them loose so they are easy to reach
questions.explanation: Weight close to the ground and equal on both sides keeps the center of gravity low for better handling.
questions.manual_quote: Distributing the weight closer to the ground and equal on both sides keeps the center of gravity low

questions.question: Compared with a car, how much stopping distance does an RV need?
questions.answer: A longer stopping distance
wrong: A shorter stopping distance
The same stopping distance
No stopping distance on dry roads
questions.explanation: RVs are heavier than cars and need a longer stopping distance. Keep plenty of room in front.
questions.manual_quote: RVs are similar to trucks in that they are heavier than cars, and require a longer stopping distance.

questions.question: When may a pedestrian start crossing on a red or yellow traffic light?
questions.answer: Only when facing a WALK signal
wrong: Any time no cars are coming
Whenever they are in a crosswalk
Only after waiting 30 seconds
questions.explanation: Pedestrians may NOT cross on a red or yellow light unless facing a WALK signal.
questions.manual_quote: Pedestrians may NOT cross on a red or yellow traffic light, or on a red-green combines light unless facing a WALK signal.
